What most people will be asking about this game is how similar it is to Civ and is it BETTER than Civ. Firstly, despite having many similarities in the type of game it is and the way it's played it is actually very different. Secondly, in my opinion it is a far better game. The rest of this review will try to explain why.
The most obvious difference is that here you have a fantasy setting rather than a historical one - which you prefer will simply be a matter of taste.
The first major positive is that you can level up heroes and give them progressively better equipment based on what you have researched. Standard units can also be upgraded in this way (through the edit unit feature). This is FAR more useful and interesting than the single purpose you can give generals/great architects etc in Civ.
The second major positive is that the factions you can choose from are a lot more diverse and different in the way you go about playing each of them compared to the positives and negatives attached to factions in Civ. This gives more replay value whilst also making multiplayer more interesting. Attached to this diversification we have the fact that each faction has its own individual quest/mission thread making single player more varied by faction also.
The unit types, whilst very different at a faction level, are quite limited. Some may find this a drawback in comparison with Civ but, personally, I find that it is more useful in both highlighting faction difference and STREAMLINING what you can produce during multi-player. Whilst this is true, you can also assimilate various minor factions (of which there are many) that may make extra unit types available to you meaning that armies will almost always be different even in games with multiples of the same faction.
Other, non-battle related, research is also limited in comparison with Civ - the research trees here are much smaller. Again, this makes multiplayer more viable and streamlines the whole process.
There ARE negatives associated with each of these improvements but also combat is more straightforward and less complex as is how you govern your cities. There is a lot less micromanagement in Endless Legend. Whilst this may be a big turnoff for dedicated Civ fans it will be a welcome difference for most players and, once again, aids in streamlining the game to make it viable as a multi-player experience.
Overall I feel that whilst both games have merits and problems and neither are perfect, Endless Legend provides a more interesting experience in single-player due to faction difference, hero use, and quest lines. And Endless Legend's FOCUS and streamlining of research, production, and city management make it more viable for multiplayer. 82%

Interplanetary is a turn based tank or Worms-like multiplayer artillery game, with the twist that you are a planet in orbit firing against other planets in your solar system. Be careful when you aim- shots that rely on the gravity of other celestial bodies may behave unpredictably when those objects are in motion! Shots bank and twist and slingshot around the sun and other planets. If you're not careful, you can even end up shooting yourself as the sun's gravity pulls your projectiles back towards your orbit!
Half of the game is the fun of watching your shots wind crazily throughout the solar system, and the satisfaction of a well fired hit. The other half is resource management, weapon development and planet building. Each turn gives you an amount of resources and energy to spend based on the number of mines and power plants you've built. Shields in turn will protect your cities and buildings... but only to a degree. Do you build more weaponry, or do you use the energy you've accumulated in a turn to send another shot hurtling wildly across the solar system towards your enemy? Do you protect your city that has taken a number of shots already, or the power plants and weaponry necessary to fight back? And those technologies you've been researching throughout the game... eventually they will lead up to a MUCH more destructive arsenal.
The game is solid, and is in a pretty decent place in its development. Currently it is most balanced with two players, but gets more and more insane as more players are added, so you can decide if you're in it for a genuine strategic experience or for a more casual playstyle that takes advantage of the multiplayer features and the ridiculousness of hurtling asteroids, missiles and lasers at your friends. Overall I think it can only get better as the developers add new content that will make each round more unique and satisfying.

Fun for a while.
Pro's:
- It's truly terrifying when a Trex is standing right over you and you're lying down in some bushes or a pack of Raptors are circling your hiding place and all you have is 5 arrows.
- The general foliage graphics-wise is not bad at all but there's a LOT of reused graphics over and over.
- I've seen the creature designs from other dino games which were awful but they put some effort into these 3 dino's. The Raptors look a little different from each other but they're still raptors.
- Water: The water graphics looked pretty clear and you make small waves when you walk through water.
Cons:
- I am sick and tired of being spawned right in the middle of a pack of raptors or a Trex is only 40 yards away. As soon as you try to leave the area, they magically know you're there. Even if you DO get out of their line of sight, they know exactly where you stopped to hide and will NEVER leave the area. You have to hope you can low crawl forever through some bushes but guess what? Even if they couldn't see you, they will follow you to the end of the earth. In other words, you either jump off a cliff and die or they kill you as soon as you try to run.
- It's you against EVERYTHING. By that I mean, if you have 1-2 Raptors hanging outside the tree that you're hiding in and a Trex comes around, they will both team up to find you. The Trex doesn't scare off the Raptors.
- No melee weapons.
- You could walk right up the side of a fallen tree but a small rock stops you from walking forward.
- No jump. As in..you can't jump up onto rocks or up cliff edges to get away from Raptors. If you can go there, so can they.
Need:
- Tree blinds or the ability to climb trees for a better vantage or better attack angle on smaller dino's.
- Jump
- Melee attack weapons
- More types of dino's
- Caves along cliffs and along the coast for hiding or shelter.
- campfires for cooking meat taken from dino's to eat for health.
- A damage/fear limit for the dino's. If you hurt one enough, they will run away but in reality, if you put an arrow directly into a Trex's eye, it should run off for a short time for you to get away.
Conclusion:
It was fun for a couple days but after killing multiple raptors and my 2nd Trex, it got boring.

I have been meaning to create a huge, in depth review of this game for quite a while, so I hope it is helpful to some new players that, hearing things said from others, may be a little wary.
The developers of theHunter and theHunter Primal, Expansive Worlds are constantly involved with educational visits and there is normally at least 2 interns at any time working in the development team alongside the regular, employed developers. The development team have also had lots of requests in the past to add dinosaurs to theHunter and had been interested in doing so in the past before, but they felt it would ruin the realism that many players of the game (a fair amount of which are real hunters). So, behind the scenes they started work on Primal, which was originally given the name 'Project Flintastek' (which according to google translates to 'Flintstones Fry', the developers are Swedish). Project Flintastek also quickly become a program for the interns to work on and quickly became a place where new ideas, gameplay mechanics and... stuff, would be worked on experimentally, after Project Flintastek was starting to look more and more like a complete game, Expansive Worlds decided to make it as a full game and started more serious development on it and thats where we are today.
Story clearly isn't the main focus of theHunter Primal, nor should it be really, this game is about hunting primarily, however it still manages to tell an interesting story, that is, if you are eagle-eyed enough to find the hidden logs and traces left by previous Pioneers and some kind of native inhabitants, or just, really loopy people. The story that we know first off is that you are sent down onto this alien world to kill (hunt) the native inhabitants, which just happen to be very similar to the dinosaurs that we know from our past. If you fail? Your close family will be offered up as pioneers themselves. So, dont fail. Whilst I say that story shouldn't be the main focus of this game, it would be awesome if it were included/integrated more, such as finding an old camera that would then play a cutscene of a settlement being attacked, or something similar. But, yeah, interesting story but sadly most of it is hidden away in log entries of abandoned old settler mates.
You will be equipped with nothing but a Machete, some basic clothing and boots as well as a map fragment, which will highlight a random settlement on your map (these are the only places to find weapons). It immediatley hits home the feeling of helplessness as you are stuck on an alien planet, with just a machete to defend yourself. However, if you are just starting out, find a map on the internet and go to a settlement. You are going to need a better gun, I would also reccommend playing only on your own for a while as this will help you get better at the game more than if playing with friends.
Within the first hour you will have certainly met your first dinosaurs and hopefully have found your first proper weapon, preferably in reverse order. This is when you will, probably start to get frustrated. This game, you realise, is hard as nails and I will admit, it is very unforgiving for new players to theHunter series or just new players in general. However, if you stick at it like I did and keep trying, you will get the hang of it and start hunting dinosaurs, instead of them hunting you.
theHunter Primal is, and dont get me wrong here, incredibly frustrating, at times very difficult and can, at its very worst feel like a chore, having to go and get your stuff of your dead body whilst avoiding what killed you. But other than that, the game is so, so enjoyable and when you finally start to get the hang of the game and get used to all of the mechanics etc... it is the most rewarding experience I have ever seen in video games, the sheer feeling of joy when you finally kill your first T.Rex or when you track down a wounded Triceratops to find it later, dead from bleeding damage and to claim it as a kill, or when you find ammo for your favourite weapon or just discover new things, these special moments are what makes the game so, so worthwile. It can also be a very eerie and creepy experience, so people who don't want to get their heart racing should probably stay away from this title... it can get so intense when a T.Rex is just metres away from you and you are just lying in the ferns and vegetation, hoping that it wont spot you and that it will just leave already, the way the ground shakes with its footsteps can be downright horrifying.
So, to put it rather simply, theHunter Primal can be frustrating, but is an intensley rewarding experience that can both make your heart race with joy, or fear. If you are looking for a survival and building game, you wont quite find that here, despite being classed as a survival game this is a hunting game truly, you won't find crafting here.
The Graphics in this game are very good and suit the tone of the game well, certain things could be done better, such as the character models and various textures being stretched on some areas of the environment, but this is a good looking game.
This game doesn't play like your typical survival shooter and actually takes a while to get used to how to use all of the functions and elements to aid your gameplay. The controls will feel slightly strange at first but you will definitley get used to it. It plays like a more fast-paced version of theHunter, the movement is faster as well as equipping weapons and items, everything is just smoother and more slick looking, so I would certainly reccommend that you go play theHunter if you are not sure about whether you will like this game, the movement etc is the same however the world and animal species are of couse, very different.
The developers have never yet missed a weekly update, except when they went on christmas holiday, which, to be fair, is totally acceptable.
The game is, admittedly, somewhat plagued by glitches that can hamper (or at times, even enhance your experience) but none of them are of the game breaking variety.
Even though the game is 'finished' at the time of writing (11/05/2015 GMT) the developers have not missed a single weekly update (most commonly published on Thursdays) that will always either contain bug fixes, new content or changes and tweaks to the existing game. The developers say that there is no guarantee of new content to be added to the game however the future looks bright. As theHunter Primal has and will continue to be not just a standalone game, but also a place for interns and the developers to test new ideas and mechanics so it is very likely that, maybe not as frequently as we have had new content recently but it is not unreasonable to assume that as things are experimented with that we will see new content in Primal.

Do you like murdering your friends? Or do you like just winning without violence?? Well, it doesn't matter when it comes to this game because you can play it both ways(also this game has friendly grinding so have fun)!! 100% orange juice is a fun(painful), and friendly(rng) board game where you and your friends(let's be honest, it's not like you have any hue~) compete against each other in order to complete your goals throughout the game. What I think makes this game 100% fun is the RNG(random numbers generator) and the unique character design. All of the characters that you can play are listed from, "hyper aggro" which means you mainly attacking the players/mobs, and to "peaceful" which thats mean you mainly farm for your goal without killing really. I personally play "super aggro" because it adds the spice to the game for everyone(also who doesn't like killing everyone to win the game :D?). The character that I use is from a DLC titled, "100% Orange Juice - Breaker Pack" which is 2.99 on steam. Her name is Star Breaker, she is one of the most aggro of the bunch that can ONLY win by killing anything only through battle. Back to the core of the characters, each character comes with their own stats. The core stats titled in the game are, ATK, DEF, EVD, and REV. ATK is your damage bonus when rolling your dice(we will get to the dice rolling later), DEF is one of the ways to protect yourself from massive damage, the second way is called EVD which doesnt only help you from taking damage, if you roll higher than your enemy you will take 0 damage! Lastly, there is REV which means revive. When you lose ALL of your health points you will go down which makes you have to roll a dice to get back up. Let's say you have 4 REV, that will mean that you need to roll a 4 or higher in order to get back up and start moving and such. But, if you fail to roll on your REVs it will go down by one. So, if I don't roll a 4 or higher it will make make me try to roll a 3 or higher the next time I can try again. Pretty neat right? Also, if you roll a 3 when attacking, whatever number is shown for ATK will add on to that 3. So if I do roll the 3 and I have a +2 ATK, that +2 will add on to the 3 which will make my attack 5 in total. Same goes for DEF and vise verse with negative numbers. NOW to the tiles, there are 8 different tiles... But don't worry, I won't type each and every tile in detail. 1st tile is a blank tile... it does nothing when you land on it. Move tile makes you roll your movement again if you land on it. Star tile makes you roll a dice to see for bonus stars upon landing. Drop tile makes you roll a dice which makes you lose a certain amount on landing. Then we have the monster tile, this tile will obviously make you fight a basic monster with the prize of some stars and 1 win. Boss tile is also obviously a tile that makes you fight a MUCH HARDER monster but with a huge reward(tip, you will lose to it a lot so prepare for it or avoid the tile unless you think you can handle it). The draw tile will make you draw a card, I won't be needing to explain that.... right? They are pretty easy to learn once you read up on them. What comes after is the home tile(oh boy I was dumb trying to learn this). The home tile shows your number depending on the sign what turn your on. Now here comes the weird stuff... IF you happen to have a high roll number or if you land on it exactly. Landing on your home without taking the rest of the tile steps or landing exactly on it will ask you if you want to stay on home for the turn. This is where you would click yes if you finish your norma(norma is your goal basically, in order to check on whats your goal hover over the character that your playing). If you didn't complete your norma but you need that heal, you should click yes and it will heal you for 1hp. BUT, lets say that you want to land on the other player's home get that clean 1hp heal and/or want to complete that norma. Heres the sad part, you need to EXACTLY roll the right amount and land on the home :(. Well, after reading this you think that you will destroy people online and bots offline... YOU'RE WRONG...ish.. the RNG can punish kinda hard but don't worry, you will still have fun right? Right...????

To begin, I always found Skyrim to be somewhat of an overrated game. I did have fun with some of the quests, but the combat never resounded with me. However, when Oblivion was recommened to me, I bought it (on sale) and was particularly surprised by the fact that I enjoyed it much more than Skyrim, despite its age.
Two points of note in relation to Skyrim (as most of you have likely played). The combat can be straight up painful at times. In most ways, it's worse for me than Skyrim. However, the magic is a lot easier to use than it is in Skyrim, and you will eventually get used to the hit boxes after a few hours of playing. Secondly, the quests feel a lot more fleshed than those in Skyrim. There's a lot less rinse-and-repeat dungeons and caves, and more variety to the sorts of things you'll be doing.
Basically, I recommend this game for the amazing side quests. If you can ignore all of the obvious signs of age (graphics, melee combat, etc.), there's a lot of golden dialogue and content that's totally worth it.

This game is amazing, even more so when modded, but we're not talking about mods right now. Though if we were, I'd have to say that Oscuro's Oblivion Overhaul is kind of a big deal. But we are not talking about mods.
Oh, where can I even begin about Oblivion? The Imperial Province of Cyrodiil is beautiful. You can go anywhere in Cyrodiil and revel in the beauty of nature, from the rolling hills of the Colovian highlands to the marshlands down by Leyawiin up to the Jerall Mountains which house Bruma, the lands that make up Cyrodiil are just beautiful. If Tamriel was a real place, I would want to live in Cyrodiil, even during the Oblivion Crisis, because I have no other words save summarizing it as beautiful to describe it and I could spend hours outside of any given town, even the Imperial City, just taking in the natural world. Sure, the graphics are no longer the greatest and the people look derpy as all get out, but if you can get past the looks of the game, you'll find one that is in many ways, in my opinion, better than Skyrim.
Let not my mere 65 hours on Steam fool you, I've been playing this game since 2009 after it was released on PS3. I know what I'm talking about. Some mechanics are less than ideal, such as gear that breaks down with use, but it is semi-realistic, nothing lasts forever, and some make no sense, such as needing repair hammers but no forge or whetstones or anything like that to fix worn out gear, but it's still a great game. I don't really like those aspects, but they're there and you will be utilizing them.
Skills work the same as in most if not all other Elder Scrolls games, use them to improve them and level up when you've improved your skills enough, and when you level up, you have the option of which of your stats to improve, though the actual leveling up part was changed significantly in Skyrim. In Oblivion, those stats are Strength, Endurance, Speed, Agility, Personality, Intelligence, Willpower, and Luck. When you do level up, you'll pick which stats to improve and they will have a boost of between +1 and +5, depending on what skills you used to level and how often you used them. To build Strength, you work on Blade, Blunt, and Hand-to-Hand. To build Endurance, you work on Armorer, Block, and Heavy Armor. To build Speed, you work on Athletics, which is done automatically as you run and swim around, Acrobatics, and Light Armor. To build Agility, you work on Security, Sneak, and Marksman. To build Personality, you work on Mercantile, Speechcraft, and Illusion. To build Intelligence, you work on Alchemy,  Conjuration, and Mysticism. To build Willpower, you work on Alteration, Destruction, and Restoration. You can improve Luck upon level up, but no skills affect its rate of growth, though Luck itself does have an effect on all skills save Acrobatics and Athletics.
I've heard some people say they reached a point where they struggled to improve their stats or skills anymore because they reached a certain level and blah, blah, blah, but I myself never really had a problem. My problem was that some skills, most notoriously in my opinion, Restoration, improved so slow when enemies you face begin casting better spells or using their weapons better than you at the same character levels. I'm not saying you have to grind, you can finish the main quest at level 1 if you try hard enough, but if you want the best spells or want to deal more damage and have different power attacks with your weapons, you may want to look into ways to grind certain skills, including abusing trainers, to get them to 100 as soon as possible. Me, I prefer spamming Light spells to grind Illusion to 100 after leaving the tutorial, usually waiting until I've bought the house in the Waterfront District. You can grind Mercantile by going through the ruin that's across the water from where you exit the sewers from the tutorial to find a Varla Stone, then going to the Imperial City Market District to talk to Calindil at the Mystic Emporium to get two of any scrolls he has multiples of and just one of another, then going into your inventory, clicking on the scroll you have two of and dropping any scroll you have only one of. This is the Duplication Glitch you may have heard of. Continue clicking on a scroll you have multiples of and dropping scrolls you have less of until you have three of one and only two of another, then just keep doing that, click the one you have more of, drop the one you have less of, pick up the ones that you dropped, and start again. Easy as that. I prefer doing so until you have 500 of a scroll for carry weight purposes. Doesn't have to be particularly good, just needs to be a spell scroll, though you may need to sell some to make 500 even. Once you have your desired number of duplicated scrolls, you just click the one you have 500 or however many of, then find and drop the Varla Stone you got in the ruin you ran through after exiting the sewer, then pick them all up and sell them to compatible merchants. That's how you grind Mercantile. Be aware, however, the stuff you duplicate will go everywhere, causing a risk of losing small things and accidentally stealing something and you will get over encumbered doing this, so work on Strength when leveling up until you've maxed it, invest in Feather spells, rings, and potions, and learn how to carry stuff without actually adding it to your inventory until it ceases to be an issue. And there's other things you can duplicate to sell to other merchants to grind money and Mercantile, including the staff Apotheosis at Rindir's Staffs, so don't think you have to keep selling Varla Stones or that you're stuck if you can't sell someone Varla Stones yet. Just find what you can duplicate and sell to them until your Mercantile is sufficient to sell anything to any merchant, then abuse the economy with duplicates of expensive items that are supposed to be one-of-a-kind. And don't forget to haggle.
And on the subject of the duplication glitch, you can permanently affect yourself with enchanted rings by doing the glitch to make just two of an enchanted ring, equipping one, then doing the glitch with just two scrolls again to the copy of the ring you don't have equipped to drop both copies but keep the enchantment. It is for this reason that I like to learn as many spells as I can as quickly as I can, then join the Mage's Guild at the earliest opportunity, for access to spell making altars and enchantment altars. Leveling up in the process of doing all this helps to get better quality rings and higher grade Soul Gems with bigger souls to return your investment, because once you've permanently enchanted yourself, you won't be able to equip those rings again. To gain those effects again, you need to equip a brand new ring, and enchanting a new one costs money, as does in some cases getting better quality rings and Soul Gems, though you can duplicate the best ones of those. Just keep one Ebony Diamond Ring and one Grand level Grand Soul Gem on you at all times so that when you want to permanently enchant yourself, you just do the duplication glitch on them and go to town. If you do, I advise doing so with Strength and Feather rings because I cannot stress enough how fast you will become over encumbered even when duplicating light things. You can do the permanent enchantment glitch on all your stats, Feather for carry weight, the ability to breathe underwater unless you play an Argonian, your Health, Stamina, and Magicka, and your magical resistances, right up to becoming immune to Fire, Frost, and Shock. I do not advise permanently enchanting your skills because in Oblivion, even with magic affecting your skills to make them high enough for the next mastery level's set of skills, you're still considered as having the lower level of mastery of your skill.

Alright, well, I played this game to see if it would be fun, like any other game, but I will admit, I've spoiled by other games similar to it. Only If doesn't have the same feel to it like, let's say- the Stanley Parable, and I completely understand that they weren't going for a similar feel or gameplay even. But, they left out things that made the Stanley Parable fun.
Firstly, I feel like the motion is very very hard to watch. I'm usually really good with fast pace games- heck, I play first person shooters all the time. This game, however, made me feel like I was running in slow motion in a dream where I can't really tell what is going on. Which, again, is part of the point, but it was annoying at times. ESPECIALLY the cutscenes. And- half of the time, I wasn't sure if I was still in a cutscene or I was given control of the keys again. Now, the imagery in the game is actually very pretty. I like how the rooms and environment look. Unfortunately though, due to the movement, everytime I move my mouse, I get a sense of motion sickness and can't really see what I'm looking at. It makes parts where you're supposed to be quick about your actions seem like a blur and much more difficult than they need to be.
Secondly, the sound needs to be improved. I had my volume at around medium and I still couldn't hear what the protagonist was saying sometimes. He mumbled a lot, which just bothered me a little. Though, I will give the voice actor credit, because I don't think that was his fault, but the game's sound volumes. Like- the "antagonist" also is hard to hear sometimes, mainly because you must be right next to him to hear him. When looking around a room and being directed by his voice, it means that I have to stand perfectly still next to him until he's done speaking, or I'm going to miss something.
Thirdly, I just didn't like the quick-time events. I know some people find them more interactive in a game, but God, I couldn't stand it. It makes your vision much much more blurry (which I understand is supposed to make you disoriented, but given that I can't move normally without somewhat blurry vision to begin with...) and while you're walking it expects you to repeatedly click one button or else you die. And you have to restart from when the chapter began. I don't like having to restart a quick-time event because of me messing up another.
Oh and can we have the chapters start at gameplay, not cutscenes? If we were given the code to start again, it should mean that we've seen the beginning cutscene already.
So, anyway, Only If is a game that has some technical flaws and so far I'm a not huge fan of it, but I can see where they were going with it. The storyline has... what I'll call potential, the acting is decent enough fo the game, and the environment is made actually surprisingly well. It's still a brand new game, but it needs a lot of work.
"In Only If, you will fail a lot, you will die a lot, and you will undoubtedly be confused. "
You sure got that right, game. But I don't like dying over and over and getting confused when trying to do the most basic of tasks. The first few minutes of the game shouldn't make my eyes hurt. Just saying.
Oh- which is why I couldn't play more than 20 minutes by the way.
I wish I had been able to keep playing too, because it sounds like Only If might have a better storyline near the middle and end, but if I can't get into a game in the beginning because of simple game mechanics, I just can't.
But, if you like this game, good for you. I can see why you might enjoy it, I guess?
For me, however, I've played better games with a similar type gameplay. And this just doesn't compare at all.
So, I won't recommend this, sorry.

Sonic Mania might just be the best official Sonic game that exists! It takes Sonic, Tails and Knuckles, back to the roots of the Genesis Era, when the games were a wide success, and when in overall Sonic was better of a video game series. The game brings the graphics back to the roots of the Sega Genesis while also being more detailed and nice.
In Sonic Mania, you can play as the same character roster from Sonic 3 and Knuckles; Sonic with Tails, Sonic alone, Tails alone, and last but least, Knuckles. If you are new to Sonic games, or just want to have your first playthrough be easier then as if playing with the others, you should play as Tails then for your first save file until you are able to play as the others, not that Tails is bad. He is a very good character to play as, given he makes getting out of tricky situations and getting on higher routes, easier then if you were playing as, say Sonic alone.
Special Stages return in the form of Catch The Ufo stages where you have to collect rings to keep the ring meter above zero, and collect blue spheres to raise your speed meter. You start at Mach 1, which is easy to control in terms of speed. You eventually get to Mach 2 which is much better. You want to keep it at Mach 1 or 2 as much as you can, because let me tell you about Mach 3, aka the Mach limit. When you collect enough, you eventually hit the limit, Mach 3. This makes everything much harder in the Special Stage due to how fast you are now. Your main priority should be to run after the UFO and collect Blue Spheres and Rings that are close to you so that the UFO doesn't get too far away from you, or else it will be harder to catch up to it. Catching the Ufo will win you a Chaos Emerald. Get all seven, and you get a achievement for bragging rights, and the ability for your character to turn into their super form! There are also other collectibles in the form of medals. You get them from the Bonus Stages, which you access from StarPosts when you have above a certain amount of rings ( amount is a low number around 20 ). These Bonus Stages are the Special Stages from Sonic 3 and Knuckles, the Blue Sphere stages. As you collect more medals, you unlock more extras such as different abilities for Sonic from older Sonic genesis games, a mode where you can have Knuckles follow your character, and more stuff like a DA Garden from Sonic CD, and Debug Mode, though most of them, you can only select for No Save runs like Sonic's abilities, Debug Mode and etc, which sucks.
Overall I recommend that every Sonic fan gets this game! Even if you aren't into Sonic anymore, give it a go! I used to be a big Sonic fan long ago when I was much younger, played the older games on Genesis, which is how this game tapped into my nostalgia, and for the most part of the game, I was nostalgic and excited! You should give this game a try!
Sonic Mania is a 10/10 game because I said so. And $20 isn't bad either so... Or buy the soundtrack for $20 instead of the actual game.

I'd like to get one thing out of the way right off the bat. This game is already one of my favorite games, and if they are able to improve on it from what they have here, and truly flesh out the mechanics and support, than this will be one of the best games of all time, hands down.
However, right now, at this time, there are some problems with it, and you should be aware of them before you consider purchasing. First off, it is ONLY multiplayer right now, be it hotseat, lan, or online. Part of this is because the game is most certainly tailored for a multiplayer experience.
Unfortunately, the game does not have a chat feature, nor a lobby feature, which means that playing the multiplayer is a bit lessened as an experience, unless you have another means of keeping in contact with your friends. Additionally, the Online servers are VERY unstable. Not everyone will be able to connect, and it's tough to determine who and where the connection problem is at.
Aside from that, the game has very little explanation text, beyond the tutorial. The tech tree needs fleshing out, with a better description of how certain things behave, and what you can expect from them.
Now for the positives.  Like a game of risk, this is a game best played by getting some buddies to sit down and play it out for an evening, forming alliances, backstabing eachother, bemoaning your losses and cheering your victories. And it certainly brings that feel one hundred percent. I've yet to be able to play a large game with my friends, but I look forward to when I get the chance to, and to see a truly dynamic swing of advantages.

Well, unfortunately, as it currently stands, this is a multi-player only game.  If I had known this, I would not have spent the money on it.  At the very minimum, this should have some sort of single-player tutorial mode, which is not currently included.  I was forced to play 'multi-player-hotseat' with no one technically assigned the second seat.  Since there is no AI for the second player, then it becomes a game where you are defeating yourself.    As to the game mechanics, it is a type of gravity sim, where you fire kinetic rocks at your openent, OR lasers once you have the tech, and your firing is adjusted according to gravitical effects for kinetic weapons, affected by all other planets in the solar system, and can be blocked for lasers by line of sight issues if there is the sun or other planets in the way.  Rules wise, it all makes sense, but as a single player game, this is a complete no go.  Sorry folks, if you don't have friends to stop by and take the 2nd seat, you have nothing to do.  If you DO have friends to switch out the hotseat mode, then you have the issue where your friend can see everything you are building even though they technically do not have the technology by game rules to do so... IE over the shoulder views of what you are doing when you are sitting in the hotseat.

A great game which is definitely worth a buy. theHunter: Primal is a survival hunting game which offers intense and exciting gameplay as you try to survive and hunt dinosaurs. I can see this game going far as it has a great community and an active development team. Whilst it is still only in early access, and most of the content is still lacking, it is still a great buy.

If you enjoyed TheHunter and wished you could have an opportunity to hunt dinosaurs with more of a suspense/horror feel to it- this may be the game your looking for. Its got five weapons as of this point in development- Bow, pistol, shotgun with slugs or buckshot, 308 rifle, and the .700 double rifle. Your prey are raptors, tricerotops, and Tyranosaurrus Rex. The game starts off very punishing as you discover alot of your movements only work to aid raptors and rexes to find you. But you get used to how everything works and soon your getting the first attacks in and eventually rounding up the troops and getting revenge on the rex that just ate you.
Seeing a rex lower its head and widen its stance to get ready to charge is downright horrifying. The stomping around as it gets closer and eventually shakes the screen with screams puts you into the scenerio of being the prey for once. Raptors have calls that you will learn as well. They have different vocalisations for when they hear you, when they spot you, and even then they plan on lunging at you.
There are some downers about the game though becuase its still early in development. It crashes alot still, often times at clutch moments right before a big takedown, or after you die, when you drop items, or during a trophy shot. Hosting a game requires you to open ports and thats annoying for many.
I still find that this game is highly addicting and worth playing. I have no doubt in my mind that many of the issues will be ironed out before its formal release. I do love this game and I've been playing it non stop. I recommend this game whole-heartedly.

I love this game. I've spent three months playing it most week nights before bed.
Interestingly for me, I alternate between completely enthralled and slightly annoyed. I've never really been able to decide whether its my decisions in the game or the game itself that causes either.
To be clear, this is an intense game. You won't pick this up and cruise through, and you won't download this game and Google-walkthrough quickly. Even with walkthroughs it's tough and random and you better be prepared to spend hours clicking on barrels and clicking through inventory and dialogue to put your characters in proper position for fights. However, the time you spend doing those tasks is overwhlemingly rewarded as you progess through the story. It's just outstanding.
You may get tunnel vision as you focus on specific missions, but then you'll misstep and discover something completely new. It'll suck you in for 10 hours before you remember what you originally set out to do. The "side" missions are not really side missions and are worth an entire game themselves. Often, I find myself thinking that it's just too much for me to even dive into with just 3-4 hours to play each day. I plan out what I want to do before I start. "I'm not even going there today. I'm just going to get my skills straight." or "I'm just going to make sure I get this where it needs to go. I'll deal with that this weekend."
The game did prove buggy at times but nothing that necessarily affected advancement. Audio channels and the actual dialogue cut out for me quite often but would usually fix itself pretty quickly. I think the toolbars could be easier to organize, but, I admit, with this many options and tools and items, I see the difficulty in design. Admittedly, I often found that silly decisions from AI kept me alive during battles. This could be intentionally designed, and I'm not complaining. I often prayed those decisions would happen. They don't always. I just feel obligated to relay my experience. I think it would be beneficial to change the gear system in a forward-thinking way, but I won't get into specifics. I don't want to alter someone's opinion prior to playing the game.
For the price, you will not find more entertainment, challenge and value than you will with this game.

Warframe is a farming game, you're gonna spend most of your time farming for resources. That's something you should know.
Besides that the game is insanely fun. One of the most impressive facts about this game is that, it's completely free, even Platinum (which is "paid" ingame currency) is free, you can get it just by trading valuable items that you get for free. However you will need some luck to get valuable items that are worth a lot of platinum.
There are Warframes which I'm going to be reffering as characters in this review. There's a prime variant for ALMOST every character. But prime and non prime variants both need parts to be crafted. Non prime characters are crafted by finding parts from (most of the time) bosses. Every planet has one boss which has chances to drop those parts.
The parts you need for characters are: Chassis, Neuroptics, Systems. After that you buy a blueprint from the market which costs free ingame currency (credits) and in 3 days your new character will be able to claim. Remember that you have slots for characters.
But it's a little bit different for prime variants. You still need the chassis, systems, and neuroptics. But you get those from relics. And relics are obtainable from Interception, Defense, Survival, Excavation, Spy and some more missions. You get them as rewards. Also the blueprints need to be obtained from relics as well. But you could also buy an entire set from warframe market (website) for platinum from other players.
Regarding the weapons, non prime variatns are crafted by purchasing blueprints from the market (or simply finding them in missions). And they're relatively easy to craft, you craft them with normal resources you get from planets.
And prime variants are the same as prime characters.
Also I forgot to mention primes are simply better than non primes.
So that was a long wall of text, but it will help you decide whether to download the game or not.
Just one more thing: The developers aren't great. They suspend/ban you based on how many reports you got, NOT because of what you did. Well, most of the time. So try not to go number 1 on the leaderboard because jealous players might report you and it's game over for you.

So it stands to say that i've played a bit of warframe. Not nearly as much as some people, but more than a few. I have also spent a considerable amount of money on "prime access" events and platinum, and i would not say that i regret any of my purchases, as i've genuinely enjoyed a lot of the time i played in warframe. However in it's current state, i cannot reccomend this game to someone looking at it for the first time.
I'll put the TLDR up front: it's buggy, hard to get into, and the cash shop sucks.
now for the nitty gritty details!
Warframe is and has always been a NEST of bugs. I cannot remember any time in recent or distant memory where i would consider this game "stable" especially on lower end devices.
Some examples:
-There was an entire period of a month and a half where myself and my roommate both had the same issue where neither of us could patch the game due to warframe's launcher not recognizing itself as online due to a clientside issue. it was patched after three seperate tickets. i co-ordinated with my ISP and DE. DE was INSTISTANT that it was my isp, my isp wasn't sure but they did everything i asked when we were troubleshooting the issue.
-Constant and consistant dropped connections in instanced matching (public.) i have dropped from an instance where the host was literally sitting less than 10 feet next to me because of latency. i pinged him and received 10ms, the average for online gaming is usually somewhere around 60.
-Menu bugging, where you can reach the end of a 30-45 minute match and have the game not be able to bring up the results page, effectively rendering that time wasted, as well as various navigational issues pertaining to the landing craft.
-Broken interactions withing the game (see below)
* Inaros' ressurection does not work 9/10 times. you can successfully fill the meter with ample time remaining but the game doesn't recognize it. i've even had occasions where i was playing with an oberon who had boosted the time remaining while downed and all it did was prevent me being able to revive!
*nidus' meter for his passive does not correctly display, and on various occasions it will stop accumulating all-together with no explanation, effectively ruining a match.
*various status effects not working as intended such as stealth or sleeping effects. you can put enemies to sleep but they will continue to be alerted to your presence, ruining the stealth bonus.
-Most recently, i decided to stop playing for a while and come back after a major patch to see if it was a little more stable. i encountered a game breaking bug within the first 5 minutes of my visit to cetus. I would consider this game volatile if not unplayable for me. this may have something to do with my computer, but i am able to play plenty of other games just peachy keen.
Aside from the bugs, the whole business model is also subpar. The ingame currency is hawked at every intersection. There is absolutely nothing in game that cannot be in some way subverted with currency.
Ranging from:
*Multiple days worth of build time for components, weapons, or warframes subverted with 50 platinum.
*Guild requirements or questing requirements to earn a specific weapon IE: Lab research items in the cash shop
*Massive bonuses from paid buffs, such as EXP/Credit boosters. these might not seem like they're as good as they are but the difference is astonishing.
The game is also super hard to get into without someone there to help you. yes, this is essentially what guilds are for, but to the level that it would take an absurd amount of time for a new player without guidance to understand the objectives at hand IE; Bossfights and their rediculously specific hitpoints, the general game progression, stats and farming locations, and don't even THINK about trials or arcanes.
SPOILERS BELOW:
The main "quest" of the game follows a questing tree that is only initiated by scanning one obscure NPC that only spawns in a very particular tileset, and this is not explicitly stated ANYWHERE AT ALL in game dialog or otherwise. i think the only thing i saw that even mentions it is a loading screen blurb, and even then it doesn't give you all the details.
I think that this is highly unintuitive for a quest that literally completely tourniquettes all progress in the game and story. i think during this period of my playtime i spent more time on google than i did actually playing warframe.
END SPOILERS!
TLDR again for those who dont feel like reading; bugs, bad-business, and hard to get into as a new player.
thanks for reading this if you did, and regardless of what you choose to do, i hope you have fun in whatever game you choose to play.

Awesomenauts is an excellent game that I highly recommend. It’s a MOBA game with a Saturday morning cartoon style and from a 2d view, yet works surprising well in gameplay. Visual wise the game is great. While playing I felt waves of nostalgia from the times I watched cartoon tapes on my VHS. In terms of audio the sound effects feel cheesy, but I personally think that adds to the charm. Each individual character has their own unique theme song and a bunch of witty one liners they shout during battle. Some characters are even voiced by famous youtubers like OMFGCATA, TotalBiscuit, PressHeartToContinue, Myndflame and HAWPofficial.
Gameplay is where the game really shines though. You, your two team mates and your three opponents pick a character. Afterward you get launched from a space ship in a drop pod which can be moved around to collect money as you fall towards your team’s base. At the base you will find the shop, which is vital. Your character has four rows total to buy from. The top rows are your abilities you must buy, and once you bought that ability its upgrade row is opened and you can use it in combat. Below them are your standard attack and utility which are unlocked from the start. Each row has six different upgrades that can be applied to the corresponding category, but you can only choose three of them. This adds depth to battle as you will have to sacrifice one thing to improve another and so on. The main goal of the game is to destroy the solar drill, which is stationed at your base. It is guarded by tough turrets, but if they are destroyed the drills open to attack. You and your team have to defend your turrets and destroy theirs, and I have to admit that it’s pretty fun!
The major flaw is unbalance of newly released characters, but that’s solely because they just came out and get patched up pretty quickly. This game is very good, and I hope buyers will enjoy it as much as I do.

Finally, there is a new Sonic game that captures everything that made the original games so great. With a single exception (a level that's a tribute to Sky Chase from Sonic 2) the player has the choice whether to take everything at top speed, or slow down and explore the whole map. Both styles of gameplay are amply rewarded. The levels are huge and have many intersecting paths, so no two trips through a level will be quite the same; and there are plenty of bonuses and secrets if you keep an eye out for ways to stray from the main path. Several extra life monitors are plainly visible but a puzzle to work out how to reach them; and even in the zones that most closely follow the original games, the locations and methods of accessing bonuses are always new.
As with any Sonic game, there will be a few frustrating deaths as you strike a moving obstacle in just the wrong way and get crushed; but overall the game is very fair and the player always feels in control. The extra lives awarded for collecting every 100 rings, combined with the large levels and frequent shields, make it fairly easy to get to the end; but there is a satisfying gradual increase in difficulty in the later stages.
The bosses are a mixed bag. Some are very well-designed and fit perfectly with the difficulty curve; others are mainly included as entertaining references to earlier Sonic games. The hardest boss in the game appears in Flying Battery, the fourth zone of twelve.
Overall, the game feels very much like the best parts of Sonic 1, 2 and 3 blended together, but made even better with a bit of hindsight about what worked and what didn't.
What SEGA should do next is keep the same team together, have them bring back even more of the classic zones, and include a level editor.

So I am only recommending this game, because these were the guys that brought us Men of War Assault Squad 2. However this game has been in development for a very long time, it has a weird free-to-play model, microtransactions, and only two factions currently. I supported the game, and by that I mean put money towards development about 6 months before the game was even announced. The hardest part about this is the fact that, all I got was a standard edition and I still had to buy a season pass. It is on the same game engine as MOWAS2, however it still looks beautiful. When they get around to adding the 64-bit client, and hopefully engine improvements to allow the maps to be a lot larger, as you have access to aircraft, I feel this game is still very early access.
I'll start with some pros and then go into the cons. The game has a really cool and really redefining first-person and third-person view. Almost like you are playing a first-person shooter and not a real time strategy when you switch into the mode, however, the time to kill is a little long even if you get hit markers, elite units, seem to take headshots with ease. The vehicle, currently being reworked, will be interesting once fully implemented. Currently it is a very lackluster roster, some basic tanks and vehicles for each side. Which I know they are adding more, but I would like to see some more diversity within the GRM.

The campaign is interesting, however I will not revisit it until the game is out. In terms of gameplay, you have such a wide variety of tools, that the game is not falling short, by that I mean that it is not worse than Assault Squad 2 as many people try to state. I believe it is the fact that the game is on par but a lot of people feel cheated as this is the next entry into the series and with all of the amazing success that Assault Squad and Assault Squad 2 brought. This game can only get better or worse. Yes that is a positive/Pro+, because there is a lot of room for them to make this game great and amazing and not just ehh. I will save some of that for my conclusion. Some other interesting features, are ones that have been shown off and are being added.
The new vehicle modular damage system, constant gameplay balancing, and I will say the fact that it is a free to play, with a grind, I feel if you have the money it is worth it. And this makes me happy because it gives people the chance to experience what I would like to call The Assault Squad 2 experience, without having to pay right now. There are the caveats, some loot boxes, emblems, crates, but a lot of it doesn't really warrant much. I see this as a positive, as they could add weapon, uniform, and vehicle camouflage, as well as patterns, that you could use the paint, and emblems, to create your own little army, something unique.
Now for some of the cons. The game is poorly optimized in the sense that the maps are tiny, it's a 32 bit client, the game has been in Early Access for a long time, and people are getting very frustrated, and either outright leaving, or being very toxic. I understand this is not the fault or the intention of the Developers, but when they state Q2 2017 as the release, and we're already going into 2018, it causes some worry.
My main negative feedback for this game, is not a long list but I will name a few things. The 32 bit client, small Maps, limited vehicles, limited infantry types, still not able to set up MANPADS/SLSAMs (dedicated anti air emplacements), the fact that we can't even set up a FOB, and many people are going back to Assault Squad 2 so the maps, either don't work, or were abandoned. My biggest gripe with this is the fact that they need to do some major updates to the engine, there are so many things that should be able to be done in game, and not the editor.
Summary and thoughts: This game has tremendous potential, if they upgrade to a 64-bit client, increase the map sizes, rework vehicle mechanics including aircraft, rework most animations as they are the same animations as Assault Squad and Assault Squad 2. I also believe that they need to add more flexibility as I stated above, when it comes to setting up a defense. This is not 2014, we have technology that allows us to fly through space simulations and land on planets, however I can't set up a small fob and defend a capture point, without somehow manipulating the editor, and even then it's more of an attack and defend. The biggest downside to this game is it removes a lot of free time that it should be giving players. You can add aircraft you can add the first person viewing, the thermal optics, all of these really amazing and interesting mechanics, but you don't allow players the ability to do most things, why can I not set up an entrenchment with a stationary gun, and I'm not talking work magical bushes grow out of the ground, what animation and physics.
My final thoughts are these, I supported the game before most people knew it existed, and I continue to, the free-to-play model allows players to play the game, what makes them work to unlock unit which I think is fair if they have not bought it.
As this is a review and not a post on a forum here is some simple feedback. Update the engine, large maps, 64-bit client, updated graphics; whether that be in engine or outside of the engine in a separate type of integrated module, give more powers to the player in game and do not make them create a map for a certain situation that they may only play one time, listen to your community... And to me this is a personal one.
*** For the Love of Christ, the Virgin Mary, and Saint Peter, some of us who do not like to play with the toxic online players, and like to play against AI, a little bit of love!!! I understand PVP is a major selling point. But I am still a buyer and I know many people like to play against AI, even if it's to train their skills, or because they're like me and work full time and don't want to wait to get put into a Lobby where half the time the other players leave, because you have bought the game and they haven't, therefore you have vehicles and infantry that they don't. I mean come on guys can we get some love in the local offline community? ***
It is true that the game is not very polished but it is an early access and with the release coming soon I am confident that this game will get even better then it is right now.

I would like to start by saying that I REALLY want this game to be good.  I know it is not exactly a triple A series, but some things just have to be added.
To start with, there aren't enough guns and attachments for people who like to have multiple options to take down enemies.
- The best example would be Payday 2.  It is also in the same category as this game in terms of subjective value.  The reason why I still play it with friends is because there are so many guns and attachments and every game is different based on the random actions of the AI.  You won't need to include as many guns as Payday 2, but 5 weapons is just not enough.  (I'd appreciate a 50 cal rifle like the M99 or M95 ;] )
-The dino variety also hurts the immersion this game would ultimately have.  3 dinos is ridiculously pathetic (sorry for harsh words, but it significantly hurts the game in my opinion).  You could start with the famous dinos, like:
+pachycephalosaurus
+pteranodon
+Parasaurolophus
+Deinosuchus
+And many others from the cretaceous period. Because there are so many to choose from, I'd add in more prey animals and I'd LOVE to see a Deinosuchus! The world needs life!
-The dino AI is borderline non-existent.  I've found myself standing in front of many dinos as I put bullets into their faces and end up taking no damage because it did not notice me.  (Also a major immersion breaker).
-The animations for turning is also a major breaker since they turn like I'm playing a Garry's Mod session.  You could look to some recent dino documenteries for examples.
-As in games like Far Cry 4, there NEEDS to be interaction between animals.  I have not seen any interaction between animals ever!  It doesn't need to be extensive since it is a hunting game, but it completely destroys the immersion for me, in addition to everything else.
-PLEASE reduce the zoom for iron sights! The use of scopes is almost useless because it has about the same zoom level as a scope, but with a better field of view.
-Another major aspect that is missing is the nests.  I'd love to stumble upon a raptor nest or some other dino's nest and be ambushed by the parents!  I do not expect parental behavior, as in hatchlings and raising babies.  It doesn't need to be that accurate.
-For the love of God please let us JUMP!  I've been stuck in weird gaps that I can't get out of because I can't jump!
-The inventory system is an OCD nightmare.  The ammo needs to be able to stack.
-The day/night cycle is choppy
It seems like i'm being harsh to the game, but as I first said: I want this game to be awesome! I had so much immersion during the first hour of playing, but seeing all of the immersion breaking things I've pointed out, I am almost unmotivated to continue to play.  I read that you guys are going to add in some structure building into the game and that would be awesome, but compared to the points I've listed, this is secondary.  What's the point of having structures if the dinos are so stupid, you could just go prone and wait for them to wander off again?  When it releases, you should do what Overkill does (the maker of Payday 2), release DLC for a reasonable price to add more content into the game.  New dinos, more weapons, more clothing, etc. Some of us are against DLC whoring, but in this case, there is so much that could be added, you'd need a triple A budget to make it a dream game.
Before I finish, I'd like to point out some things you did well in:
+The detail on the dinos are very well done.
+The way noise works is simulated well
+The way loot works is good for the environment you intended to make, though I'm not sure if the loot pertains to who ever takes it first.  PLEASE DO NOT MAKE US FIGHT FOR THE SCARCE SUPPLIES!!!
+The guns feel good, could be better, but I do not expect perfection in this case.  (if it's a $60 triple A game, I expect near perfection)
+The sounds of the dinos are also done well and made me shift into stealth mode many times!  I love it!
+The animation for the T-rex is good, but I've never been lifted up as the animation suggests,
+The bleed out is good, you've done this before anyway.
+The hand signals or emojis are done well! I appreciate those things because it helps boost immersion.
+For an alpha build, this runs very reliably, possibly due to the simplistic nature of the game in its current state.  it could use some refinement in terms of optimization, especially if you are to add all of the things I've listed.
+The ambient sounds really helps with immersion!!
I really hope you find this helpful and I hope you add at least some of the things I've listed.  If you do, I'm definitely going to convince my friends to pick up the game and purge the island of beasts!

Oh boy, this is my new game.
So Divinity Original Sin 2 is a tactical role-playing game, and boy am I glad to have more of these around, I have a bad history with standard RPG's so this was good for me. Combat revolves around trying to get the upper hand against your enemies, whether that be by utilizing terrain advantages, using crowd control skills to prevent enemies from moving or acting, and all around everyone is trying to screw everyone else over.
I did not play any previous divinity games, but I don't think it's required to appreciate the story. I think the game is best played in co-op, because you and your freinds will constantly be in a state of fighting each other to see who's the best, in arenas and at the end to decide who's worthy to become a god, just don't be the one friend who blames the game when their fighter/pyrokinetic/scoundrel duel wielding one handed sword and dagger summoner can't beat everyone else. You think that example was made up, don't you?
So the game is quite difficult, for the most part. You have the choice of Explorer mode, Classic mode, Tactician mode, and honour mode for difficulty. Beware, because Tactician mode and up the game addopts the philosophy of bigger numbers means harder, it's a lazy way to increase difficulty, they should have focussed more on giving enemies buffs and new skills, which is noticable but not as predominant as the massive bloated numbers. Seriously, you and your three freinds could be wacking one enemy for six turns before they die, but if you can do that you've already gained control of the fight, so you won long before they go down and the whole fight has a feeling of being forced. Combine that with late game, where they just throw a bunch of enemies at you and it becomes waiting for your turn simulator.
Overall the game has tons of content, the Origin characters have detailed story lines that intertwine, there are tons of skills, tons of stats to upgrade, tons of my run-on sentences, you can make every fight different with terrain effects and synergies, and there are tons of ways to make your freinds♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥at you. You have tons of choice with diologue options, you get to pick two "Tags" for your character, which help you determine who they are and where they come from. Over the course of the game you can pick up the "Hero" tag by being heroic, or the "Villain" tag for being a jerk, both open up even more options to screw with people, be a knight and shining armor, and all around have a fun time with my run-on sentences.
I highly recomend this game, one of the best games I've ever played

Divinity Original Sin 2.
TL;DR: 6/10. Get it on sale.
The bad:
Writing: The writing for this game is muteable at best. It and NWN 1 share the 'main campaign is♥♥♥♥♥ syndrome. I do not like any of the NPCs, any of the quests or any of the plots. It lacks feeling, everything is so gray and cliche.
Barrel mechanics: The game is oversaturated in environmental hazards, most notably barrels. I feel these are to the game's detriment and I am loathed to see them no matter where they are.
Game mechanics: They're not very satisfying. It's over-saturated in magic, conditions and punishes you for being tried-and-true melee as opposed to being any sort of spellcaster or ranged combatant. Even the monsters are throwing magic. Quit that. There's also physical and magical armor, that halves damage and... huh? It's more convoluted than any of the DND rulesets prior to 5E, as someone who's played them religiously for a decade.
Lack of direction: The game sort of just... plops you in and expects you to find your way. The NPCs you do talk to basically mumble about nothing worthwhile before dropping bread crumbs of a quest in their mumble and expecting you to unravel it. Your friend? Where? Who? What? Where do I find them? Who are they? What were they doing that got them captured? Elaborate. Give me something to go on. But lets say for the sake of it that you decide to play along and actually adventure around trying to find what they're talking about. I personally could not care any less about the actual adventuring aspect, because the terrain is the same old ugly terrain that puts me to sleep to just look at it. It suffers from 'everything is samey and bland' syndrome, like Path of Exile.
Camera angles: Ungodly awful. To swivel and look around with it is a headache. Two different buttons just to pan your camera? Neverwinter Nights one called, they said they want to loan you the driving camera.
Bugs: There's so many bugs. NPCs will randomly turn hostile (even if you did nothing to upset them, no thievery, no nothing). Sometimes in the arena beneath Fort Joy, you'll beat all of the combatants. If you're playing with friends, you'll have to fight each other for dominance. Even if you win (or lose), sometimes you'll just be stuck roaming around the map because it won't pull you out, and you'll have to reload. The bugs steadily become worse and worse by act 4.
Poorly planned Multiplayer: The ability to play with three other people is a nice gesture, BUT, to play with them, you'll have to start with them at the very beginning. You can't introduce a character mid-game and have them scale up or down to the main character's level. Otherwise, you'll have to play some limp gimp premade NPC who the main player probably uses as nothing more than a loot mule and a bullet sponge.
----
The 'meh'
UI: It's serviceable. It's not great, often times the chat box will get stuck where you're trying to click. Sometimes, when you're trying to control an NPC, it won't completely register what you wanted to do, and instead your character who's at the top of this post will instead abandon his post to chase a barrel.
The soundtrack: Generic Latin-lite choirs. It is so bland it is incapable of being offensive to the ear. It is unspired and to be truthful, I did not care for it.
Art Design: The game is bland and grey on the art design as well. Nothing jumps out and impresses. The cutscenes in which drawn characters do battle or things of that sort look far better, but the game itself is just... meh. It's clear that the armor was intended to be little more than just shapes to tell who was who when zoomed out at full capacity.
----
The good:
Initiative track: The game has a functioning initiative list, where you can join battles mid engagement, as well as ensure everyone has a fair turn. NWN had one of these but didn't truly work.
Moddable: Like Neverwinter Nights, you can mod the game to high hell and back, changing a lot of the problem I had with the game.
Custom modules: You can completely ignore the primary campaign and play different modules. There is also a DM feature, in which the DM can control NPCs, create pieces on the dot, make them talk and onwards. Much, again (if you haven't seen a running theme in comparison) like Neverwinter Nights and to the game's favor.
-----
Final verdict: The game is serviceable as an RPG, but not very fun to play. I believe the future of this game does not rest in the production of the company, but rather in the hands of the community.

Recommended.
Story...
The title of this game hints to a story, perhaps to a story on a deeper level. It sounds like the game would happen between two deities who both want something. That sounded extremely interesting to me. While I didn't expect too in-depth background due to the type of this game, I was still disappointed by the lack of it. There are exactly two cut scenes, at the beginning and at the end. The title mislead me quite well for making me believe something particularly exciting would happen between the packs you have to finish.
Characters...
There's not much to the characters and that's not really surprising. Still, the two main characters (and I use that term loosely) have a connection to each other. It's hard to tell what kind of relationship it is, because they never, even once, speak. So in that as well, the characters lacked depth.
Gameplay...
It's very simple, but nice nonetheless, if you know what to expect. I expected the Fever Mode to be a timed version of the main game, but it's not. You have a certain time to finish a mosaic and you gain more time every time you finish one. So you can go on as long as you have time. It was a pleasant surprise for me, since I typically do not like timed versions. It was a nice add to the slower, more relaxed version. If you start with a Fever Mode, maybe the game mechanics work differently? That I can't say.
Art...
When you first begin the game, the main screen has BEAUTIFUL art. It was gorgeous, and had quite sharp details. The colors were wonderful too. It was pleasant to look at and I expected it to apply to the whole game.
But. I was once again disappointed. The cut scene animations don't have similar style at all. Admittedly, animations rarely look as good as the main art. But the level dropped down a lot, almost made it look ugly. Visually appealing games are my thing, so to be first introduced to an amazing view and then to have it change... It was a true shame. The only good thing is, that there were only two cut scenes.
As for mosaics, all of the packs had different textures. From glass-like to rough, it was interesting - and some of the textures made the gameplay more challenging.
Music...
I loved the music. It hit me immediately when I began the game. I actually wished that I could listen to it some more, which is rare for me. I liked the main tune the best, but the others were quite pleasant to listen to too.
Conclusion...
I enjoyed this game enough to recommend it. It might typical to this type of game, but it has a good soundtrack, mosaics with different textures and two modes. Achievements were nice and not too hard to get. And it's not horribly pricy either.

From the moment I first tried the free demo, I understood that this game is going to be one of my favourites. So buying it for Christmas was one of the easiest decisions ever!
This is easily the most visually stunning "jigsaw type" puzzle games I've ever tried. Each group of puzzles mimics a different material - stone, paper, glass, etc. Unlike in an ordinary jigsaw, the puzzle pieces vary in shape and size.
At the start of each puzzle, about a fifth of (randomly selected) pieces are already placed on the board, and it's up to you to place the rest. There are 3 game modes. In Normal mode, you can get a maximum of 3 stars. The first for completing the puzzle; the second for not making any mistakes; and a third for completing it within an allotted  time. The Relaxed mode is similar, except you get a third star even if you don't complete it on time. There the fun part is trying to beat your own personal best. The Fever mode presents you with nearly-completed puzzles which have only a few pieces left to place. There the task is to complete as many puzzles as you can within the allotted time. The final puzzle in each set is circular - the challenge there is figuring out how to rotate it to fit the non-rotating puzzle pieces. And for me it's a hard challenge indeed! All those variations mean that the replayability is near-infinite. The difficulty curve is admirably smooth too!
The music in the game is very Zen, helping the player to relax and concentrate. Although some people might find the same 3 tunes repeating over and over again quite maddening :)
As I said earlier, the starter pieces are selected randomly and vary in shape and size. Some pieces very unique, like the sun or the arm of some pixie; others are harder to figure out. The thing is, the "tray" at the side only shows 5 pieces at any  one time. So the speed  with which you are able to complete a puzzle depends to a very large extent on how lucky you've been with the pieces you get at the start. Some people call it a drawback; I welcome it as an added challenge. There's always a Restart button, after all :)

So I couldn't sleep and I was looking for some new puzzle games and I happen to find a freebie game tagged as a puzzler. Well, I wouldn't call it a puzzler. But is strange, oddly compelling, and despite not being a very good game worth a playthrough just to bask in the oddness.
In essence this is just a collection of odd scenarios that just often barely count as a game that are tied together by the premise of you character getting harrassed by "vinny" who only speaks to you through a radio. These back and forth conversations are played off for laughs, but are mostly nonsensical, juvenile, unfunny, and seem to have been recorded without any real script or intended purpose. Which, coming into the game knowing nothng about it kind of heightens the surreal nature.
The gameplay mostly involves walking around somewhat pretty environments waiting for a hint to tell you what to do. A few segments are a little obscure, and a few points require platforming which is really just awful to perform here, but generally you're either told exactly what to do or it's obvious. Nothing to solve really, but that's not the point. This is weird for the sake of wierd, which is to say, download this, wait until you've completely forgotten why you have this game on Steam and play it at two in the morning one night when you can't sleep.
If this wasn't free I probably wouldn't recommend it, but it is so it's worth a shot.

I have been playing this game for years, since it was just Crusader Kings, and I have to say it has always been my favourite Paradox game. CK2 only improves what was a great concept and game and refines it into one of the most unique historical titles you will find anywhere. While combat in Paradox titles always plays out in a fairly simple manner, combat is never over-simplified. There are many options that you can (and should) work on to have a highly trained, well-equipped and well-balanced armies. Your ruker and family can be trained to follow a martial career from a young age or you can promote people outside your family to lead your armies (which eventually you will have to).
It's the family mechanics and dynamics that are so fascinating though. You try to establish a powerful family that is interwiven in the ruling houses or Europe, Middle East, Northern or Southern Asia through marriage, children, inheritance, etc. Throw into the mix a blend of diplomacy, intrigue, betrayal and revenge, and you have the major elements of CK2 (but so much more... the game often plays out like a novel, and is every bit engrossing... with the Age of Charlemagne DLC, you can start your rule in the Dark Ages in any realm of your choice and play until the age of Columbus. At that point, if you haven't had enough scheming, warring and empire-building with your family, you can export CK2 to Europa Universalis IV (I believe) and carry on your quest for glory into the Age of Napoleon (who may or may not end up existing, depending on the makeup of continental Europe by that time.
All in all, a fascinating and engrossing game that is not to be missed by history lovers. Most of the DLC really improves the game experience too and makes it much more immersive.

The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion is the IVth installment in The Elder Scrolls series. A simple looking game on the surface, but one that holds many hours of entertainment for the players of all types. The Elder  Scrolls IV: Oblivion's main quest see's the player working to remove the portals of Oblivion from the land. These portals, numerous in number, and all equally annoying, lead the player into the Rhelm of Oblivion, literally hell, just called something else.
Each of these Oblivion planes are swarming with nasties, like Scamps and Dremora Churls, all incredible pains in the neck. Should a player be fortunate enough to survive Oblivion, they will be awarded a Sigil Stone, and the portal will close, allowing the player a sense that they are accomplishing some great task.
This however is not the case, as if you play like someone such as myself, then you are well aware that Oblivion is not a threat in the slightest to the population of Tamriel. In fact, if you come across an Oblivion portal, you can simply waltz right past it and get on with more meaningful tasks, such as collecting herbs for your potions, or finding new gear to sell.
Oblivion also allows for some incredible character customization. If you check my screenshots, you will see an example of what the game's character creating engin is capable of. Furthermore, the games "modscale" console command can see players disturbing their friends with horrific acts of size manipulation.
Also, this game includes the well known, and much loved "Adoring Fan". If you are going to buy this game for any reason, this is it. The "Adoring Fan" is a "groupie" who "worships the ground you walk on". This is not only any sane persons dream, but is also a very easy quest to achieve. Furthermore, the developers are Bethesda very wisely gave the "Adoring Fan" one of the most annoying voices in the game, and some of the worst quotes.
I strongly recommend this game to anyone who wishes to delve deep into the soul of Tamriel, and see what life was like, before Skyrim came along with their dragon born's and their .... well, dragons and a different setting is basically the only difference between Skyrim and Oblivion....
