This game is utter trite.
Now that that's out of the way here's why! :
Graphically the game is just like Men of War Assault Squad with a modern tinge to it, nothing really large scale in terms of how things look has been changed most of the buildings are the same Clay / Stone huts that one could see an artist lazily piecing together due to a time constraint.
Moving swiftly to gameplay, the gameplay is for lack of a better word, frustrating. This game is supposed to be a Men of War title, but instead it feels like a terrible mod made specifically for those with gargantuan erections at the thought of two squads of 5 fighting in high wall cover with full automatic machine guns. The worst, absolute worst, part of this game for me was what they did to the by now legendary manual control mechanic, it's horrid how they've implimented it, the third person manual control now sponsers a massive obnoxious and screen consuming bright green hud meant to "assist" with your aiming but only ends up gobbling up the screen like a monster from a bedtime story.
The absolute madness these devs have to charge people 30 U.S.D. for this game is disgusting, It is hardly complete too. In it's current state it doesn't have fully destructible buildings like in Men of War, it doesn't have any semblance of balance with the U.S. for the most part being vastly superior leading up to when the opposing faction get's it's elite units, then suddenly even U.S. Navy Seals can't fight a rag tag group of "elite" muslim extremists. There's also a very sub par unit roster, in Men of War we had machine gun teams, mortars, anti tank guns, light tanks, etc. Now obviously this is modern combat and I understand such classifications might not be there for the sake of keeping the game "realistic" but why do they have such a limited roster of vehicles. For the U.S. the majority of your "tank" equivallents are APCs with anti tank weaponry strapped to them, how is that a tank? you could've at least tossed in a Patton or something not a Striker Mobile Gun System as the answer to a T-80. Other than the poor unit roster the units themselves are so odd in the way they function. Infantry have various types like U.S. Army, Marines, S.E.A.L.s etc, but they all play just about the same, the only difference is the rate of fire it seems.
All in all this game is missing quite a lot, it feels like an extensive cash grab made by the Men of War devs who at this point have given up on actually trying and simply want to make their "Call of Duty" RTS equal. And it's absolutely baffeling the development process for this game, first they charged you for the tip top premium package or the standard game, now they've got that and a free to play system.. what on Earth are these devs thinking?
I'll leave you with this, it's a poor game, a poor attempt at recreating a money making machine, and I'd suggest personally just buying Men of War Assault Squad II, it has everything this game doesn't and then some.
Also the game has been in "Earl Access" for what, three years? and the progress they've made is making a free to play version of the game with no major fixes or updates. What an absolute joke.

Now that I've dumped 30+ hours into this game, it's time for a review.
Let me start off by saying, I was REALLY hesitant to buy this game, and read lots of reviews before I did so.  I've played a lot of survival MMO games like this, and a lot of them turn out to be unfinished abandoned garbage, but some do turn out great.
Keep in mind this game is in Early Access so this review may not be accurate at a later point in time, and they may have fixed more of it by then.
PROS:
-Fun to play with friends or just make friends online and play with them.
-TONS of skills to level up, and you can combine them any way you want.  You want to be a master of Unarmed Combat whilst also being a Fisherman that's buff as ♥♥♥♥ from Logging?  Do ittttt.
-Tons of time can be put into this game, if you're really looking to go ham in the play-time.
-Lots of items and gear and loot to find/upgrade.
-The devs are really good about fixing bugs within the first couple days of people reporting them, as far as I've seen.
CONS:
-The biggest con for me is this:  The devs announced EVERYWHERE that they were making the map 4x+ bigger than it previously was (I had not played the game previous to this 4x update), however what they actually did was make it 4x bigger and block off 3/4 the new map with impenetrable fog, so you can't go to those areas anymore. This caught me by surprise - I rarely feel engaged by 4x games (outside of Civ), but this title really has merit.
Let's get the basics out of the way - it looks great. The artistry is top-notch. The UI is fluid, and importantly doesn't waste your time with animations that freeze your ability to navigate. Everything is responsive and satisfying.
The minor factions are a great addition - something Civ struggled with all the way through 5 (with the city-states). Endless manages to make the minor factions feel "just right", and conquering/parlaying/bribing them is a huge part of the game. Plus it's just plain fun to sometimes gain their trust through quests, and sometimes through conquest. Every option feels equally viable, you can't use just one strategy to get what you want.
The major factions are varied and (again) satisfying. Each one plays entirely differently, but not so differently that you feel like you're stuck re-learning the wheel. Some games with multiple factions make it seem as if one or two factions got all the developer's attention, but these factions are well-rounded.
I could go on, but overall the game is remarkably well thought-out, well-executed, and engaging. I don't often play 4x games, but I'd feel comfortable suggesting this to anyone.

This game is everything I had hoped Warlock: Master of the Arcane and Elements would be.
The game at it's core is a 4x strategy game. You build towns and armies, develop them and conquer the world or become the world's leader through the several other victory types. However the implementation is better, with clever changes to many of the mechanics:
Combat is handled through tactical battles on the world map. Once hostilites start an area of the map is sectioned off to be used as the battle field, allowing you to know the terrain beforehand. though exploiting that is a little difficult. Rather then precise commands you give broad directions or targets in combat, which makes battles quick and brutal compared to other 4x games with tactical combat.
Towns hold a territory/province stopping town clustering though town placement is very important since the town only gathers resources from ajacent tiles, though extractors can be built on far away strategic or luxury resources. Additionally provinces have minor factions who can be convinced to join you via quests or bribes, or wiped out and built back up. These minor factions provide free workers and can be incorporated into the empire to give faction wide bonuses along with new units.
Units are quite customizable. You can choose from a few different armor and weapon types that vary depending on the type of units. The factions only get a few types of units which can then be customized to fit different roles and more unit types can be gained from the minor factions.
The factions themselves have quite a bit of variety from some factions which don't take food, to others that can't declare war, to another that cannot not be at war and even one that can only build one super town. Factions can also be customized, though the default factions seem to use more points then you get. Additionally the factions have interesting backstories that are fleshed out more on their faction specific quests.
So far the only real complaint I have is that the game is not balanced towards large maps. Expanding is punishing until high level techs are researched making much of a larger map unused. Otherwise this is probably the best 4x game I have played in awhile.
Velocibox is hard, but it nails the fun you want out of this kind of game and there's a rewarding sense of satisfaction to getting further.

I enjoyed all 142 hours spent in Divinity Original Sin 2 (DOS2). I can tell the developers really poured their hearts into this game. Every nook and cranny of the gameworld has been fleshed out with detail. The dialogue is the best I've come across. The voice acting is phenominal and garners emotion. There are a plethora of surprises hidden in even the smallest sections of the gameworld, some that can go on for hours at a time. I never became bored with the combat and enjoyed the limitless possiblities - especially since stat points of party members can be re-allocated at any time. I also really liked the art style of DOS2 and the graphics are among the best offered by an isometric RPG.
Another huge plus with DOS2 (and DOS1) that I got a kick out of was the level of gameworld manipulation - both physical and environmental - that can be performed with the many abilities party members possess. Need to heal? Bless a pool of blood to create blessed blood that heals party members.
The only slight detraction I had with DOS2 were some performance issues. This game does not run perfectly with quad core  cpus and often times ineffeciently utilizes the cores causing degraded performance. The seriousness of this issue was not enough to interrupt my good experience I had with the game however.

I'm gonna be crucified by this game's fans, but Warframe isn't that good and it's kinda Pay2Win despite what people say.  I do not recommend it even though I had some fun.
I've put almost 200 hours into this game and everything is just a blur of flying down hallways at 200 mph and spamming E to throw swords at people.  There was exactly one quest that was memorable and that's only because it was a giant surprise that you'd never see coming unless you go and read spoilers.  Warframe is fun, but it isn't the kind of fun that you'll remember the next day.
There were a lot of little things that turned me off this game, but the biggest issue I had was that I always felt like I was being used, like the developers were scamming me.  You constantly have to grind specific areas or using specific gear in order to unlock the things you really want to use...
Your "Mastery Rank" in the game is your account's level and it determines which weapons you have access to among other things.  You raise your Mastery Rank (MR) by levelling up weapons to their max rank.  You level up weapons by using them.  However, you have to craft each weapon, and you only have like 6 weapon slots to start with.  So if you want to level your account, you have to go through this ridiculous process of:
-Grind for materials
-Craft weapon
-Wait 12 - 24 hours (of real time!) for weapon to be done crafting
-Level up new weapon by using it (possibly to grind for materials)
-Trash the weapon that you waited 24 hours for and spent an hour levelling because you need room for the next weapon.
-Rinse and repeat until you master enough weapons to reach the next MR
After you go through all the work of crafting and using a weapon, you just throw it in the trash because you need to make room for the next one, and it feels terrible every time.
Oh! But if you spend some real money, you can get more weapon slots. And you can buy the weapons pre-assembled, no waiting!  Hey, the game is Free right?  Don't the developers deserve some money?  You're not doing it for yourself, you're just throwing them a bone, right?  You'd spend the time to grind out the weapons anyway, it's not like you're getting any advantage, RIGHT?
tl;dr: Warframe is fun to play but the developers are honestly scum for devising such a system.

I am positively flashed by this game. I had fun with Warlock: Master of the Arcane and stumbled with Heroes of Might and Magic. I was appealed but bored by Age of Wonders III, but this Endless Legend...
I went straight in without going into the tutorial first. Exploring this wonderfully complex ressource and economics system that is untypical for this genre of Fantasy 4X allows a play style for everyone - which leads to war being the faster and in early difficulties the more viable solution. However, war is not always the same. While each factions is pretty much unique and has access to their very own units, minor factions and tribes can be indoctrinated to fill the roles you need. Which is awesome. Endless Legend gives freedom to the player and I commend this game for this bold, but very well executed move.
Endless Legend does a lot of stuff right. It has its minor mistakes, for example: You can have multiple AoW-styled battles going at the same time, but you can't properly move two armies the same path. Moving units out of cities required one button click too much - and sometimes they leave by accident. But these minor complaints from my side cannot possibly compare to the gorgeous experience, lore and mashup Endless Legends provides. I mean, Dragonpeople fight against Fallout-Style Vaultpeople, Magicians and the Scourge.

People sometimes overlook games because they seem to convey an impression of "Been there, done that." In other words, concepts, ideas, mechanics, etc that have been used or done before. At first glance, Endless Legend does indeed have those traits. But, when settling in to give the game a chance, there's a feeling of refresh by the way it presents itself.
The graphics and style of the game are beautiful and help give a lovely sense of immersion and personality. The music score of the game is especially a treat and only help accentuate on these features. Gameplay is refined yet still deep enough to be somewhere in the intermediate of complexity. No, it's not the most deep of strategy 4X experiences one could have, but that's certainly not a bad thing. Rather, the way it plays out allows one to still use their mind and strategize, but not be overwhelmed to the point where it takes hours and lots of reading to make heads or tails of how the game plays out.
The factions in the game all have their own background, theme, traits, and their own thing going for them. And I have to say, some of them are downright intriguing. And in some cases, even unnerving--but in a good way! What's nice about these factions is they all play quite different from one another and even have their own quests to follow. As such, one could play through the game and have a distinctive experience each time. Though, this is all also thanks to the many customization options one can do for the world generation, changing anything from size, terrain types, general land formation, world difficulty, victory conditions, and more. For those bold or wanting to mix things up, you can even make a custom faction based on one of the existing ones as a template.
Combat is turn based with light tactical considerations. It's not as deep as some other 4X games, but there are some I have played where it's even more simplistic than how Endless Legend presents it. As mentioned before, Amplitude seems to aim to make games that have a happy medium with their approach to complexity, nothing too complex, but not too simple. They also like to make a nice clean, accessible, and slick interface to help make navigating and display information in a pleasant fashion that helps make a person feel comfortable using it more than intimidated.
I do like the direction Amplitude has been going with their games and certainly would love to see future developments from them. Their work is pretty solid from day 1 release. Though, there are bugs to be had and their track record with patches has been quite good with Endless Space. As such, their support is quite good and they're willing to do what they can to make their fans happy, even if given some time.
Bottom line, if you like 4X strategy games and enjoy ones of a fantasy nature that doesn't take itself too serious, but not too lackluster, I think you'll be at home with Endless Legend. It's a happy medium that makes it hard not to like for those that aren't looking for something too complex or casual.

More empire building focused than AoW, faster paced than civ and takes all the best mechanics from Endless Space. If you're familiar with the Endless lore, there will be lots of 'Ahhhhhhhh' moments as you realise which factions are like the Endless Space factions (there is continuity).
Overall it's a pretty strong 4x game - there's a lot of victory conditions (including a main quest), and every faction plays differently. The factions are designed well and while I couldn't debate balance with you, all of the factions are fun to play (♥♥♥♥ the cultists though - my minor faction towns are MINE GO AWAY). Some of the factions are actually designed by community users, too; pretty sure that's the cultists again.

Wow, this game is just a breath of fresh air in an age of sequels and recycled gameplay.  I've been playing through this almost exclusively co-op with a few friends and it has just been one of the best co-op experiences I've had in a long time.  I can’t really think of a comparable quality story driven, co-op RPG on PC since maybe Neverwinter Nights and that is 15 years old.
I really like the fact that everyone is free to run around and do their own thing and have their own conversations without generally locking the party into cutscenes or anything like that.  You can choose to follow your companions around and listen in on them, or you can split up and report back what you've heard in your own conversations.  Not having control of your character usurped every 5 minutes for an unskippable cutscene is quite nice.
Over the last few years, I’ve played some Dungeons & Dragons on Roll20, Skype or Tabletop Simulator.  Playing through this game feels very much like the D&D experience, even borrowing many of the mechanics like passive perception and attacks of opportunity.  Both in and out of combat, the game gets a lot right in this regard and really shines as a result.
And speaking of the tactical turn-based combat, it is really great.  I’ve mostly played it co-op with friends, but I played the first little bit single player as well.  Either way you go it is very fun, and can be quite challenging at times if you get in over your head.  And you can’t just eat a lot of deaths either because your resurrection options are limited, at least early on.
A lot of the combat revolves around elemental mechanics similar to that of Magicka.  So for example you can spill oil on the ground, ignite it with fire, put the fire out with some water thus turning the water into steam and then you could shock the steam cloud and make it electrified.  This makes for interesting situations in combat and there are often unintended side effects if you are not careful.
The combat AI of the opponents seems passable enough.  I have seen them do some pretty questionable things at times though.  In particular, during one fight we had an enemy archer spend 2 or 3 turns shooting arrows into a barricade because it didn’t have a clear shot at our rogue.  There have also been a few other instances where they would take actions which seemed to benefit our side more than theirs.  We’ve only played on the ‘classic’ normal difficulty though so I can’t really comment on the higher difficulties.
The controls can also be a bit tricky at times, leading you to accidentally move when you intended to use an ability or vice versa.  But this mostly just comes down to being patient and paying attention to what you are doing.  If you try to do things too fast before the animations finish it can mess you up.  Also the game won’t tell you if your ranged attack (bow/wand/staff/etc) will hit something in the environment so you just need to be aware of things.
Although I’ve somewhat taken a back seat in the story development process in our play through, the fact that all the interactions with NPC’s are voice acted really helps.  And while every side quest isn’t Witcher 3 levels of amazing, I haven’t had any complaints.  You can even take a perk and talk to the animals if you want to be just a little be more depressed along the way.
All in all I have been thoroughly enjoying this game and would gladly buy an expansion or another sequel in this series.  I look forward to future releases from Larian Studios and hope they can continue to provide truly phenomenal games without all the shady modern business practices like endless microtransactions and loot crates.

I wrote a review of this game around 2 years ago when I first tried it and gave it a mixed review, saying it was fun but I disliked the matchmaking.
After spending some more time in game and paying closer attention to how the mechanics work my view has changed enough to rewrite this review, so here goes.
First, the game is funny. The dialog, the improvised weapons, the character models, pretty much everything is designed to give off this vary silly feeling. I mean you're playing as a group of psychos who run around pretending to be Batman or the Joker, shooting each other.
Pretty much everything (save for a few things like 3 costume sets and some the mascots (which do nothing)) can be gotten in-game throuigh grinding. It takes a while, but it can be done. The DLC are only there to make it faster, and nothing is really OP there since they're all in game anyway. So as far as F2P goes this is a pretty fair business model.
Matchmaking is decent, but there are no dedicated servers, so connectivity can be spotty and you might get dropped depending on various factors.
As a shooter there's not much new here outside how some of the gadgets work, but the rest is par for the course in FPS titles. The guns don't have a lot of recoil, but you still need to be mindful of effective range.

I will make a quick note that I was one of the those players who played this game when it first came out. I wasn't one of the original backers back during the beta testing, but I was one of the players who tried the game back in 2013. Back then I would have given this game a solid 5/10, simply okay for a F2P game. The action was great and the graphics back then looks nice, but the lack of content and frustrating controls were the downer. After years in development, I was curious to see how far this game came along, especially when I heard about the Plains of Eidolon. I was actually quite stunned how much this game improved from its responsive controls, tons of content, beautiful graphics, and the action was still fast paced as ever. Honestly, this is one of the best F2P games I have ever played. Although this game is still a total grind fest, it's not so bad if you know what you are doing. A friend of mine who put about 2200+ hours into this game definitely helped me out a lot getting pass the initial time gating and the grinding. So I didn't have a hard time going through the grind, but I know a few friends who have gone through the initial slugfest. Although I hear they did make it easier to grind and increase mastery levels unlike before. To those who are wondering, my Mastery level is 13 and I am currently working on getting to 14.
Q: How does the game run? Any bugs or crashes or technical issues?
A: In my first 100 hours of playing I rarely encountered any bugs nor any crashes which is a good sign. After I reached the later stages in the game, I've been encountering more bugs than usual and it was beginning to be frustrating. Nothing truly game-breaking, but rather annoyance that gets in the way of your match sessions. For example, Warframes getting stuck on obstacles, specters getting stuck on things, infinite freeze slowing duration, and many more. None of them will stop you from enjoying the game; just your patience gets tested every time it happens.
Q: Do you recommend it or not?
A: I absolutely recommend it! It's one of the best F2P games out there with a lot of content, slick gameplay, tons of variation and that collector's feeling of trying to get everything in the game. I had a lot of fun with this one and I am willing to come back to it from time to time whenever I want to play a fast-paced ninja combat.
Overall score: 8/10
Pros:
+ Fast-paced, slick, smooth gameplay that makes you feel like a complete badass ninja, with so many weapons and frames to choose from to vary the play style.
+ Great looking graphics with great looking aesthetics in the models, art, map design, and clans. I can even argue that it can compete with AAA titles when it comes to graphics.
+ The sound design is mostly very good with crisp sound effects and a decent soundtrack. Nothing too memorable with the exception of Second Dream theme.
+ Fantastic customization for your weapons and your chosen frames. Clan and ship customization is fun while a bit limited, but making your frames look somewhat unique and sharing with your friends is a big delight. The developers put a steady amount of cosmetics into the game for you to mix and match styles.
+ Majority of the community is very helpful and friendly with only a small handful of awful players. The developers are very engaged with the community and they are very laid back with their community. They like to have fun as much as we do and that is awesome! They have a good customer support and should keep at it!
Neutral:
= The Story has been just "okay" it did not impress me nor did it disappoint me. I can't say much because I don't want to spoil anything. I'll just put it simply as the initial story was interesting, but resolved too quickly with little to no tension, then the story is non-existent until you reach Uranus. Second Dream was great! But War Within was kind of disappointing. The other story quests where you get frames blueprints and from Cetus are a nice distraction. The game has a fantastic and interesting lore backing the overall story, but there are still many questions unanswered. So we will just have to wait for the developers to add in more in the future.
= The time gates in this game can be extremely annoying and can make new players feel like they are not making much progress, especially when they have a very limited amount of slots to increase their mastery level. I can wait 24 hours for my next mastery test, but failing it once makes you wait 24 hours again which is ridiculous. Some items in the foundry take way too long to finish and it is obviously enticing to spend platinum to speed up the process. This game likes to pray on your impatience. Now this sounds like a con but it's not too bad because you can actually play this game from start to end without spending a single cent. If you play smart and take your time with the game, you don't even have to buy platinum. You can even trade platinum with other players, since that's how the game's economy works. If you are impatient then this game can get really annoying and almost scummy aftertaste to it, but if you plan ahead and be patient then it will always work out for you.
Cons:
- Lots of bugs to encounter, especially in the later part of the game, Though some people might not experience it as much as I did, but there is a reason why it's called Bugframe by some.
- Extremely repetitive mission design. Although the developers have made a lot more variation this time around, but a lot of the planets have the same mission structure. This also doesn't help when there isn't a lot of good enemy variation in the factions. I have seen the devstreams and the developers are going to add more unit types for each faction so who knows? In the future the game will have a lot more variety in the enemies. Currently, the game lacks good enemies or bosses. Sorties doesn't really count as adding to the variation or unique in the gameplay. It is challenging and fun with friends, but it's still the same thing over and over again with different conditions.
- PvP is like non-existent, the feature is there, but the game is so unbalanced that I've tried it a few times and did not enjoy it all. Some weapons and frames are far superior than others, making some of them obsolete. I hope DE will someday work on improving the Conclave and make it a viable option alongside PvE.
The neutral and con points looks to have more detail written for them, but that's because I am hoping the developers would someday fix these problems. I am probably missing a few more points for them, such as the balancing issues, but that can be resolved with tweaking. I have to say I thoroughly enjoyed this game and would love to see it grow some more, with an active community and developers I think this game will get even better. It's still very rough around the edges (very rough) but it's still a gem worth taking a look at.

The problem with Velocibox, as opposed to the most relevant comparison for most people (Super Hexagon) is that the overall control responsiveness is too slow, and this is in large part because the game runs at a uniform speed throughout rather than 'accelerating'--a bizarre design choice, since it limits what the game can offer. This reduces Velocibox to a memory game.
Super Hexagon generally allowed you to save yourself early-to-mid on patterns if you twitched fast enough... it was only late pattern that your pattern reaction had to be perfect, and even then a superb twitch reaction *might* still bail you out on a bad early decision or a misread. This provided both an incredibly rewarding feeling as you then fought to resume flow, and allowed you to learn levels as you progressed without destroying you immediately.
Velocibox, in comparison, is completely pattern dependent, and you'll often find yourself crashing on what seems like a flip you had ample time to make (I found the sluggishness of the control speed excessively irritating). In that respect, it becomes both frustrating for the average gamer and makes learning the levels far harder and less rewarding. The game ends up being, in a sense, only half the game that Super Hexagon was--appealing only to those who enjoy the pattern memorization aspect.
That's fine... and if that's your kind of game, more power to you... but it isn't nearly as enticing or satisfying as Super Hexagon (and yes, Velocibox's gameplay goes back to far earlier referents on the PC (even the old Star Wars vector arcade game), but I can't remember the 2 or 3 'tunnel' games it references).

This game... BOI! This is exactly what they call a blast from the past. Basically, a game made from fans to fans since it was made some of the same people that were (and still are) working on the Sonic 2 HD, crafted to be the true sequel to Sonic 3 & Knuckles and made in a way it could be considered as a Sega Saturn title. (If you ignore the fact the Saturn can’t run 1080p)
To being with, I must tell one of the best things you can get from this game is the experience of discovering the new things by yourself, since you’ll lose a considerable part of the fun if you, as an example, know all the bosses, etc. So, it’s really not recommendable for you to look at reviews of this game since they’re very likely to be filled with spoilers. (Not about the story, the story of this game is as simple as it can get, which is totally fine for a side scrolling game) And you don’t need to read steam reviews to know this game is amazing, unless you're living under a rock into bottom of the sea.
About the game play this game feels exactly like Sonic 3 & Knuckles, which is exactly how it should be. (None of that Sonic 4 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t) The momentum, the gravity, everything works perfectly.
The graphics of this game are amazing even though, as I already said before, the game was meant to look like a Saturn title, which is the reason why the 3D models of this game look like they came straight from the PS1 era. The pixel art just looks so freaking great and the animations are basically astonishing from how smooth they feel.
The sound track of this game is also outstanding and almost as good as the soundtrack from Sonic CD. Yes, I said ALMOST. Sorry Tee Lopes… I fukkin love you man, but I don’t think it is humanly possible to create a soundtrack better than the soundtrack from Sonic CD… The JP/EU one at least. (No homo btw)
About the Stages… BOI they sure are fantastic. Just like the ones in Sonic 3 & Knuckles they are full of alternate paths, which means lots of places to look for the Big rigs… I mean, Giant Rings, which are back from S3&K. There aren’t many bottomless pits. (Thank god, I’m still traumatized from trying to beat Sonic Advance 2. Bottomless pits… everywhere…) Same with the places where you can be crushed to death. (I mean, there are actually many in Zones like Lava Reef and Metallic Madness, but my point is that if you’re careful enough you won’t die.) You certainly won’t be one hit K.O.’d many times, but it will still be the reason of most of your deaths since die from regular enemies is sorta hard since there are rings in everywhere.
The Stages of this game (or Zones) are mixed from remixed stages and completely original stages, which all of them (or at least most of them) feature gimmicks or enemies from other classic games of the Sonic series. Like the Chemical Plant Act 2, which features gimmicks from Wacky Workbench, (Sonic CD) Oil Ocean Act 2, which feature gimmicks from Sandopolis, (S&K), the obvious reference to Sky Chase Zone in Mirage Saloon Act 1 (Sonic/Tails exclusive zone), etc
One thing that I find lame is the fact not all zones have stage transitions. Some simply do, some simply don’t. Something I didn’t like at all because it’s just lack of consistency for me.
Now the Bosses… they are also amazing and super creative. Sure, not all of the are good, I personally dislike the Press Garden Act 1 Boss and find the Metal Sonic boss battle really lame. But the ones that are good are REALLY good. The Hydrocity Zone Act 1 Boss though… Hell, some even are even references to games that aren’t even from the “main series” like the one that is a Mean Bean Machine match against Eggman, the Mirage Saloon Act 1 Boss (Knuckles exclusive boss) which is a Boss from the Game Gear series, the mini Metal Sonic that we fight during the Metal Sonic boss fight, which is also from the Game Gear series and even Fang, Bean and Bark (from Sonic The Fighters) that we fight against in the Mirage Saloon Act 2 Boss.
Some of the bosses are the same bosses we can find in older games but with different moves like the Green Hill Act 2 boss, the Metallic Madness Act 1 boss, the final form of the Hydrocity Act 2 boss, etc.
The Special stages of this game are also nice. They are actually my favorite special stages from the classic series (Yes, I consider this game as one of the classic games) since they’re challenging but not too hard (unlike the ones in Sonic 2. Man, I wish I could like this game more but unfortunately its special stages and Metropolis Zone are a thing.) I can consider them to be actually really fun to play. They are basically a mix from the Special Stages from Sonic CD and Sonic Heroes but using the graphics from Sonic R (They are not the exact same 3D models featured in Sonic R, they are just similar) and with a little bit of practice they turn out to be really easy. (Something that is not possible in the special stages of Sonic 1 because this crap is more about luck than skill)
The bonus stages are also back but instead of the ones from S3&K we got the blue sphere stages which are there to unlock extras. Although they don’t give you ring/score bonuses, which is a shame.
You can find those Giant Rings around all the Zones and Acts (even in the final zone) and they’re usually hidden inside walls (just like in S3&K) and they’re not much hard to find. Just require a bit of exploration and if you have lesser dead brain cells than me you will manage to get them all (the emeralds) in your first playthrough without much trouble.
The Super Forms are also back (None of that “you can only go super in the final boss” ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t) and they’re as powerful as ever and thanks to them you can rush an entire zone in less than 2 minutes and defeat bosses faster than they can do anything to try to harm you.  (You still can be crushed to death, so be careful about that.) The Hyper forms are not in this game (sadly) but this time Tails can go super without needing to catch 14 emeralds. Tails won’t have his army of super birds though.
The difficult of the game is not very high. (Maybe I see it like that because I’m a Sonic nerd and played all the classic main games 100 times each before) The game is definitely easier than Sonic 1 and Sonic 2 but harder than Sonic 3 (Since in Sonic 3 you can find so many lives around the map you can literally reach 100 lives easily) and is basically as hard as S&K.
Although this is the classic sonic game that more uses the Robotnik Monitors (which were introduced in Sonic 2 (multiplayer) and could be found in S3&K but still incredibly rare to find)
Talking about the monitors, all the ones you could find in S3&K are back but in addition to the Shield from Sonic 1 and Sonic 2 which, unlike the Aqua Shield, don’t do nothing but prevent you from losing rings once you get hit and the Combine Ring, which were introduced in Knuckles’ Chaotix that make you drop larger rings when you take damage, making easier to collect them back. (In which can be used as an exploit to get a free extra life by taking damage while having over 100 rings and collecting the large rings to re-obtain the rings you did lose and getting a 100-ring extra life for free)
The game is actually well polished and you won’t find many glitches. But there’s some weird stuff that happened to me while playing it, like the music of the Press Garden Zone Act 2 stop playing, (Which is a shame since this track is great) the Mirage Saloon Act 1 boss not showing up (Making me have to restart the zone) and the color of the super forms glitching (like Super Tails going from Orange to Red instead of from Orange to White). There are also a few glitches related to the gamepads not working but I honestly blame steam for that, not the game. The Big Picture fukkin sucks.
In an overall, this game is basically in my list of favorite games ever and worth every single cent. If you like platforming games this title is a MUST BUY. Better than Sonic Generations and even better than♥♥♥♥♥♥♥anime thighs! YES, I SAID IT!

Ok so you want to know if you should by the game or not, maybe your on the fence about it. You might want the 4x gameplay or just somthing like civ. Well im a huge civ fan and endless space fan (company that makes endless legend)
Heres what the game is in a nut shell. Its a fantasy version of civ. simple. If you like Civ, you will like this game. Now weather you love it or not is a different story.
Let me start with the cons:1.  My major gripe is the same complaint i have about endless space. the city building  just lacks the appeal you might want. It doesnt seem like you have to choose what to build in each city like u might see in games like total war or in Civ. U just reaseach it and place it in the city. Basically its like OOOOHHH new building, click and build no matter what . I would much rather have certain building that arnt allowed to be placed if u built somthing else. for example. maybe i cant build a dust mine inside the city wall if i was focusing on agriculture. Maybe the city has to reach a certain population before i can expand into another industry.
2. The city menu lacks little details like acutal population size. I would love to see political partys somehow play a role. (im only nit picking here.)
3. WARNING! (this is not a con for everyone) When in combat you dont always have 100% controll of your soldiers, somtimes they choose what they beleive is the best option. you might say run, instead they choose to fight. you have more control than you did in endless spcace (where you selected cards to give bufff but the battle was total AI control) but its not full controle
~~~~~ Personally i like this style of fighting. i like not having full control. give it more of  realistic aspect. i always use to say i wish in civ 5 instead of large units, there were map sized ones that would build defense and attack on their own stragety, u just told the gernal where to attack. This game kinfa does that.~~~~ (sorry if i explained that poorly)
4. Unit custamization. major disapointment coming form endless space. i have to carefully choose each gun type, armor, dropship, power cell, how many of each to give myself a bonus over my enemy, it made me study the battles carefully. the unit upgrades dont really exist anymore in detail, minor teir upgrades are avaible but no where near the depth of their other games.
Ok sorry really 1 major complaints. city management.
what are some of the pros
1. that maps are huge, and beautiful. tones of explortation, little in game quests that feel true to a nation building game. you can zoom in close to see the grass or zoom out and have a political style map to see the world (well done guys)
2. battles. so i already said i like how you dont have full controle but there is somthing amazing they did. unlike any nation builder i have seen, combat doesnt take u into a load screen. well tactical map style combat. If you have played endless space, strom frontline nations, age of wonders three, rome total war (not fair example just makinga  point). when you enter combat you hit a loading screen, then enter a tactical map where u can see the units fights. This game doesnt do that. you stack armies like you would in endless space or old civ games. you can choose a general to lead them. now when u go to enter combat, a border appears on the world map (the thing u see in all the images, u see cities and all that) and every army in that border enter the fight. the soldiers run out of the general and dispearse in lines within this border. other armies that are within the fighting border spawn in as reinforcements. the camera will zoom in and some grpahics like trees turn into flag drawing images so u can see the units clearly but till know if ur men are in the forrest. when the battle ends. the remaning soliders run back inside the general unit, the graphics like trees come back, camera zooms out, border disappears and you continue on. Ultra smooth and great experiace. keeps the flow but it also tricks ur mind. you become less tired of playing the game since there are no breaks like loading screens. ull logg alot of hours
3. city building. yes i want more management but the game but be praised for its improvements over endless space. the city expansion by population is great. you can see your city grow and expand. little details like the highway graphics, differnet burrows of the city, it all adds to the experiance. now there are territories, each territory or region can have one major city in it. along with ur major city, there will be minor factions that have little cities or towns. u can take them over or adopt them into ur empire and give buffs for the region and even recuit their special units.
-----also as your population increases u assign workers to help produce dust(money) food industy or science. its like civ worker menu in advance gameplay
4. detailed tech tree. Its not as strong as endless spaces but its better organized and  as u adance, u unlock new eras like civ which give u new tech. simple but organized.
ok so i tried to sum up alot  and hopefully this kinda puts u in the right direction on weather to buy. This company is a great company, they arnt greedy, their games arent expensive, and the DLC is fair. If you like 4x, or nation building like civ give it a chance its worth it. If u want the detail battles like war or age of wonders, this might not be your game.
---but if you were to ask me would your recommend this game, i would say yes. i recommend the game and the company.----------

BaK is a classic RPG like no other (except Antara, which is a poorly written knock-off). The unique gameplay and superb story makes this game worth the few bucks it costs to get it in the library.

I got this as part of a bundle with 90% discount.
In my opinion, even at full price it is worth the money. I have already spent many hours playing these 2 games. Both run perferctly on Windows 10, I had no problem whatsoever.
Betrayal at Krondor is a classic old school RPG, comprised of 9 chapters, a must play for RPG fans. The first 3 chapters and the 6th are open world, the others are limited to a specific part of the general map.
I enjoyed each chapter very much, the skills of the characters (e.g. melee) can be improved by reading relevant books available in numerous shops in various towns, by paying NPCs for lectures or by fighting enemies. Special skills, like haggling or barding can be constantly improved by bying items in shops or by playing the lute in taverns.
There are new battles to be fought in each chapter and special enemies in a few chapters (e.g. in the Dimwood forest, Chapter 7). The combat system is turn-based and a successful outcome depends on careful planning, cooperation of the fighters and their skills each time. The player controls 3 characters in each chapter, usually 2 fighters and 1 magician, but this balance changes in the last 2 chapters, when 2 magicians take the lead (helped by a fighter).
Finally, there are exquisite word puzzles, which must be solved in order to open word locked chests with valuable items. One of the best aspects of this RPG, if you ask me!
As for Betrayal in Antara, I am at Chapter 2 as of writing this review. I don't think it's as great as Betrayal at Krondor, but nevertheless it's an interesting and story rich RPG.

The collection is a fantastic turn-based RPG with a open world and a good story. The game deson't hold your hand and is considered an old school RPG. The days, when you just had to figure stuff out and pay attention to the lore. The game has only one problem: the graphics are sometimes blurry, but nothing gamebreaking. If you like oldschool rpgs, you will love this Betrayal collection.

First of all, despite of what some of the other reviews say, I have Windows 10 and it's running well.
About the games:
Betrayal at Krondor is one of the best RPGs ever made. Of course you cannot exspect up-to-date graphics, but apart from that it features character building by skill system, inventory, item durability and most of all an intriguing story which will have you chained to your screen for hours.
Don't exspect it to be a game that guides you like modern RPGs. Explore! The quest log is called PEN AND PAPER, take notes! Don't exspect to be overpowered from the beginning, your chars will suck at first, you have to build them! If you're not yet spoiled by games that are way to easy, then go for it!
Betrayal in Antara is the "sequel" to BAK. It offers very similiar gameplay with improved graphics, some new features (e.g. spell research) and a new story in a different setting. Right now i'm playing chapter IV and the story is still developing. Looks like a big political plot going on. Not as good and not the same nostalgy-factor as BAK, but also a good game.
If you can handle old games, it's a must have.
If not, leave it!

This is a review based on my experience with the game and experience with it from GOG gaming, which it seems to be the same dosbox setup so it will work here too.
For starters, I love the games enough to buy it on steam too. Krondor is the best of the two IMO. Krondor alone made it worth the 3.59 I paid. However, you need to understand that this is not a remaster, it was made around 20 years ago. This is just dos boxed so that it runs on modern computers. *trust me, it was a ***** to figure out how to run it before this set up on my own.*
Krondor is a epic story with many aspects that modern RPG's lack. Its not a short game. The graphics were phenomenal back in the day. The bad reviews are based on people expecting this to be a 'retro' game made with current tech. Its not. My biggest recommendation is to come into this game with the expectation that your gonna need to look at the manual, or a wiki for some of the game mechanics. I suspect things like the traps could be confusing for people. But, the story and the control of how your characters work, grow and some of the amazing things you can do in this game is in depth and worth experiencing even if you have to live with old tech. If you love RPG's, give this game a try.
Antara is newer and lacks a little of the flavor that I feel in krondor, but a good game none the less.
TLDR Krondor came out in 1993 and this is not a remaster, but I still place it at my TOP 5 games of all time even with the dated sometimes painful graphics.

I grew up with old school Sonic games and I continued to love Sonic even through the most troubling of phases. When I heard about Mania, like many old school fans, I was overjoyed about it and greatly anticipated it!
Mania is very well-made. I can feel the love Christian and the rest of them put into this and I commend them for living the dream and making the game they wanted.
Which brings me to my main problem with this title. It IS the game they wanted to make and play, and in being that, it shuts out all new Sonic fans and alienates those of us, like me, who grew up playing the older games but never necessarily finished them.
Mania is constructed exactly like an old school game--no dialogues, no tutorials, just you and the controls you learn on the fly. In many ways this approach works, and since I was already familiar with them I had no problems there. But while it's constructed like an old school game, it's not built like one. What I mean by that is, when I would play Sonic 2, I remember being able to breeze through at least 5 stages before getting stuck, and the bosses had a progressive difficulty to them that made sense. Mania lacks that.
In playing Mania, while I am getting old school nostalgia from it, I also find myself being frustrated regularly with it. Stages are laid out in confusing ways that don't make a lot of intuitive sense so I'll end up getting stuck somewhere for a few minutes. The stages themselves have no sense of difficulty progression at all. Flying Battery Zone really, really didn't need to be the 3rd stage here when it was the, what, 7th or 8th in its original game? And the final boss of Sonic 2 really, really didn't need to be the FIRST BOSS IN THIS GAME. Like I've said, I grew up with Sonic 2 and played through most stages when I was little, but I never beat it. I never beat any of the old school games. So when that boss happened in Mania, I had no idea how you were supposed to beat it, because the level before it didn't serve to teach you the mechanics of how to beat it. Several times I thought about putting the game down forever because it seemed unbeatable until I finally looked up a guide and learned the strategy that the first level didn't teach me!
Christian and all of them have made a great game, that I will admit, but in playing Mania it becomes very obvious that they didn't use basic game design principles while making it. Instead it's like a fan made Mega Collection with official endorsement. Perhaps that was the point, but it wasn't the game I saw advertised. Your players should not have to constantly put down the game because they get frustrated with the difficulty curve and lack of logical progression. I can't tell you how many times already I've stopped and started and stopped and started because either a level or a boss was seemingly unbeatable. This isn't an issue of not being "gud" it's an issue of bad level design and progression. The entire reason I'm writing this review now is because I just had this problem yet again today in Stardust Speedway, after having not touched the game in a few weeks.
A challenge is fine, but I as a player shouldn't feel like I need to basically strongarm my way through a game just to beat it.
So, tl;dr:
--Pros--
- Graphics are beautiful
- Music is AWESOME
- Controlling multiple characters is cool
- Controls are mostly pretty tight
--Cons--
- Poor level design (levels don't teach you how to beat the boss like in real old school games)
- Horrible sense of progression
- Bosses often make no sense (final boss of Sonic 2 is the 1st boss in this game? One boss randomly throws in Mean Bean Machine???)
- Difficulty curve that alienates most Sonic fans
- Autosave where? If I get stuck on an act 2 boss and exit it makes me complete THE ENTIRE ZONE (act 1 and act 2) again which only adds to the annoyance
But overall, this isn't a bad game. If you're an old school fan, I highly recommend giving Mania a try, just be aware of the issues I pointed out, lest you end up like me and be stuck on the first boss for days. Enjoy the nostalgia trip for what it is.

This game... BOI! This is exactly what they call a blast from the past. Basically, a game made from fans to fans since it was made some of the same people that were (and still are) working on the Sonic 2 HD, crafted to be the true sequel to Sonic 3 & Knuckles and made in a way it could be considered as a Sega Saturn title. (If you ignore the fact the Saturn can’t run 1080p)
To being with, I must tell one of the best things you can get from this game is the experience of discovering the new things by yourself, since you’ll lose a considerable part of the fun if you, as an example, know all the bosses, etc. So, it’s really not recommendable for you to look at reviews of this game since they’re very likely to be filled with spoilers. (Not about the story, the story of this game is as simple as it can get, which is totally fine for a side scrolling game) And you don’t need to read steam reviews to know this game is amazing, unless you're living under a rock into bottom of the sea.
About the game play this game feels exactly like Sonic 3 & Knuckles, which is exactly how it should be. (None of that Sonic 4 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t) The momentum, the gravity, everything works perfectly.
The graphics of this game are amazing even though, as I already said before, the game was meant to look like a Saturn title, which is the reason why the 3D models of this game look like they came straight from the PS1 era. The pixel art just looks so freaking great and the animations are basically astonishing from how smooth they feel.
The sound track of this game is also outstanding and almost as good as the soundtrack from Sonic CD. Yes, I said ALMOST. Sorry Tee Lopes… I fukkin love you man, but I don’t think it is humanly possible to create a soundtrack better than the soundtrack from Sonic CD… The JP/EU one at least. (No homo btw)
About the Stages… BOI they sure are fantastic. Just like the ones in Sonic 3 & Knuckles they are full of alternate paths, which means lots of places to look for the Big rigs… I mean, Giant Rings, which are back from S3&K. There aren’t many bottomless pits. (Thank god, I’m still traumatized from trying to beat Sonic Advance 2. Bottomless pits… everywhere…) Same with the places where you can be crushed to death. (I mean, there are actually many in Zones like Lava Reef and Metallic Madness, but my point is that if you’re careful enough you won’t die.) You certainly won’t be one hit K.O.’d many times, but it will still be the reason of most of your deaths since die from regular enemies is sorta hard since there are rings in everywhere.
The Stages of this game (or Zones) are mixed from remixed stages and completely original stages, which all of them (or at least most of them) feature gimmicks or enemies from other classic games of the Sonic series. Like the Chemical Plant Act 2, which features gimmicks from Wacky Workbench, (Sonic CD) Oil Ocean Act 2, which feature gimmicks from Sandopolis, (S&K), the obvious reference to Sky Chase Zone in Mirage Saloon Act 1 (Sonic/Tails exclusive zone), etc
One thing that I find lame is the fact not all zones have stage transitions. Some simply do, some simply don’t. Something I didn’t like at all because it’s just lack of consistency for me.
Now the Bosses… they are also amazing and super creative. Sure, not all of the are good, I personally dislike the Press Garden Act 1 Boss and find the Metal Sonic boss battle really lame. But the ones that are good are REALLY good. The Hydrocity Zone Act 1 Boss though… Hell, some even are even references to games that aren’t even from the “main series” like the one that is a Mean Bean Machine match against Eggman, the Mirage Saloon Act 1 Boss (Knuckles exclusive boss) which is a Boss from the Game Gear series, the mini Metal Sonic that we fight during the Metal Sonic boss fight, which is also from the Game Gear series and even Fang, Bean and Bark (from Sonic The Fighters) that we fight against in the Mirage Saloon Act 2 Boss.
Some of the bosses are the same bosses we can find in older games but with different moves like the Green Hill Act 2 boss, the Metallic Madness Act 1 boss, the final form of the Hydrocity Act 2 boss, etc.
The Special stages of this game are also nice. They are actually my favorite special stages from the classic series (Yes, I consider this game as one of the classic games) since they’re challenging but not too hard (unlike the ones in Sonic 2. Man, I wish I could like this game more but unfortunately its special stages and Metropolis Zone are a thing.) I can consider them to be actually really fun to play. They are basically a mix from the Special Stages from Sonic CD and Sonic Heroes but using the graphics from Sonic R (They are not the exact same 3D models featured in Sonic R, they are just similar) and with a little bit of practice they turn out to be really easy. (Something that is not possible in the special stages of Sonic 1 because this crap is more about luck than skill)
The bonus stages are also back but instead of the ones from S3&K we got the blue sphere stages which are there to unlock extras. Although they don’t give you ring/score bonuses, which is a shame.
You can find those Giant Rings around all the Zones and Acts (even in the final zone) and they’re usually hidden inside walls (just like in S3&K) and they’re not much hard to find. Just require a bit of exploration and if you have lesser dead brain cells than me you will manage to get them all (the emeralds) in your first playthrough without much trouble.
The Super Forms are also back (None of that “you can only go super in the final boss” ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t) and they’re as powerful as ever and thanks to them you can rush an entire zone in less than 2 minutes and defeat bosses faster than they can do anything to try to harm you.  (You still can be crushed to death, so be careful about that.) The Hyper forms are not in this game (sadly) but this time Tails can go super without needing to catch 14 emeralds. Tails won’t have his army of super birds though.
The difficult of the game is not very high. (Maybe I see it like that because I’m a Sonic nerd and played all the classic main games 100 times each before) The game is definitely easier than Sonic 1 and Sonic 2 but harder than Sonic 3 (Since in Sonic 3 you can find so many lives around the map you can literally reach 100 lives easily) and is basically as hard as S&K.
Although this is the classic sonic game that more uses the Robotnik Monitors (which were introduced in Sonic 2 (multiplayer) and could be found in S3&K but still incredibly rare to find)
Talking about the monitors, all the ones you could find in S3&K are back but in addition to the Shield from Sonic 1 and Sonic 2 which, unlike the Aqua Shield, don’t do nothing but prevent you from losing rings once you get hit and the Combine Ring, which were introduced in Knuckles’ Chaotix that make you drop larger rings when you take damage, making easier to collect them back. (In which can be used as an exploit to get a free extra life by taking damage while having over 100 rings and collecting the large rings to re-obtain the rings you did lose and getting a 100-ring extra life for free)
The game is actually well polished and you won’t find many glitches. But there’s some weird stuff that happened to me while playing it, like the music of the Press Garden Zone Act 2 stop playing, (Which is a shame since this track is great) the Mirage Saloon Act 1 boss not showing up (Making me have to restart the zone) and the color of the super forms glitching (like Super Tails going from Orange to Red instead of from Orange to White). There are also a few glitches related to the gamepads not working but I honestly blame steam for that, not the game. The Big Picture fukkin sucks.
In an overall, this game is basically in my list of favorite games ever and worth every single cent. If you like platforming games this title is a MUST BUY. Better than Sonic Generations and even better than♥♥♥♥♥♥♥anime thighs! YES, I SAID IT!

NEW PLAYER ADVICE/TUTORIAL
If your starting divinity as a new player, heres some advice before you start running into the game head-on thinking this is skyrim; as you will add to the list of players claiming this game is way too hard on classic mode...
No spoilers here btw.
STARTING THE GAME
At the very start of the game you are asked to create your character (sorry, spoiler!). DO NOT RUSH THIS PART OF THE GAME. Before you even look at building a class, or rushing into the game, the classes in the game develop over the course of the game, so your playstyle with said character will also change. This game is very slow and methodical, not unlike a game of chess; you have to plan ahead and think through your actions, there is no timer!
For players that have come from COD, or Diablo etc. this is not hack and slash, so you cant just run in head-on; its like sending your king and queen in to try and kill the pawns as fast as possible. try to think about what will happen each turn, and plan 2 turns ahead.
SAVE OFTEN
pretty much self explanatory, but you get jumped a lot, so safe often so that you dont have to retrack the past 10 mins of walking around.
READ EVERYTHING AND SPEAK TO EVERYONE.
This is probabally the best piece of information i can supply, and without revealing too much. divinity is about tactics not hack and slash, so speak to as many NPC's as possible and explore every area. this will grant you more experience and access to more items. As the enemies in divinity are all level based, this will allow you to stand on equal footing with them, rather than being 3 levels; wearing a loincloth and wielding a knife on a stick (actual weapon, sorry spoiler!) against a group of 7 decked out enemies all positioned in highground and chokepoints. Also reading enemies weaknesses and levels/armor etc. will help you to control fights better.
YOU DONT HAVE TO GO THAT WAY!
Many situations you come up against will look pretty damn scary, especially when you realize the enemies ounumber you, outflank you and outlevel you. This usually means you are underlevelled for the area you are currently in, so go back and complete a few more side quests, or just try taking a different route and coming back to said area (hint, you might not even HAVE to complete that area, but this could mean it holds some good items, and more levels!).
WHAT IF...
This is the most important question to be asking yourself during the course of the game, and will mean the difference between winning a fight with 0 Deaths, and losing a fight without killing a single enemy... analyse what you can do, what can happen if you do it, and how your opponent can respond (sorry this is vague, trying not to spoil anything). abuse the terrain and your opponents limitations!
TO CONCLUDE
This game is as difficult as you make it, which is why a large group of people find it so difficult, because their game is half complete! turn every area upside down before you move on, as there is probably about 3 quests you missed with 2 levels of xp. And DONT RUSH CHARACTER CREATION! Dont be ashamed if you start a new game after playing for an hour on your first playthrough, i did, because i realised i missed so much and learnt what i was doing wrong. Good luck and take your time!

I am a huge fan of the "Endless" series of games, and Endless Legend is no exception.
The game economy/resource management is very close to civ. Hexes produce food, industry, science, and dust (aka money) and you can assign workers to focus on producing one resource over others. There is no culture, but instead a resource known as influence allows you to take several diplomatic actions.
There is a large amount of customization in the game. You can tweak the base races with a point buy perk system. You can also modify your units with various weapons/armors/trinkets.
Each race is unique and thematically cool.
The combat is tactical and based around army/squad type mechanics, where if a fight breaks out units in nearby hexes will join on future turns as reinforcements.
The hero system is great as well. You can have heroes lead armies or assign them to improve your cities.

For those on the fence:
--I would not recommend this game unless you are new to a 4X title or are a fan of Endless Space.  What follows is a critical review of a game I honestly wanted to enjoy (ergo, I bought it).
This game is not one of tactical battles, but of empire-building.  It most closely resembles Civ5, but with a few minor differences:
+This game allows you to equip commander/governors and further shape your empire's bonuses.
+It also has you building small armies of units, vice each being its own hex.
-On the downside, combat is resolved in a horrible fashion, with only initial choices being made as to where to place your units, what "stance" they should take, and then who they should attack (if able).  There is rarely any reason to not just attack one enemy at time, and you are largely a spectator once combat begins.  Not being able to issue "true" move commands during a battle greatly hampers the experience and actually yields a system that is even less engaging than Civ5 (a game that is combat-lite to begin with). This is not a Gettysburg simulation, so abstraction in orders does not fit and simply comes off as over-simplification.
-UI is somewhat cumbersome, with right-clicks backing you out of menus at times and other times expanding information.  Getting heroes transferred between governor and commander requires creating and army, then shifting the hero the university, then shifting them to the army.  Should have been one button (maybe I missed something).  Other items are similarly hidden and I would recommend YouTubing Tokshen's channel to see a decent LP of it first to get a handle on things.
-You have to research diplomatic processes such as parley and bribe, as if they were tech rather than natural extensions of logic.
-There are only two seasons: Winter and Summer.  Would be interesting if expanded on, but just results in shifting population around to make the most of it.  Lack of a Spring or Fall makes it seem random and gamey.
-Artificial time mechanics.  I hate "timers" in games, and this one has the seasonal, the Empire planning (every 30 turns), and technology tiers instead of trees.  Ended up clicking through many turns to heal units, pass the winter, or wait for unneccessary techs to complete to get what I really needed.
-No world-map or commander skills to use to change things up.  Most "fantasy" stylings have magic or leader skills, this one has nothing.  Ends up feeling stale and predictable.
On the bright side:
+No crashes during play.
+Multiplayer was smooth with no issues connecting over Steam via invites.
+Simultaneous turns means less down-time waiting for the CPU to process its moves in between and a quicker game overall.
+The game is aesthetically pleasing (looks sharp) and resources "pop" out when you can utilize them, but blend in well when not available.
+Races play quite differently in the sense of what is available and when (Drakken have diplomacy, Flyers have tech, etc), as well as how resources are utilized.  Again, most of this happens on the strategic level, but is well themed.
Overall, this game doesn't do anything new and that which it does, has been done better elsewhere.  If you must have a fantasy variant, I would recommend Dominions 4, Eador, or Age of Wonders instead (in that order).  If you already own those and just want something new, go ahead and give it a try.  Similar to Endless Space, it seems these devs don't know how to do combat, just focusing on trying to reinvent the wheels of research and expansion without truly improving them.  Awkward is the best description.

"Velocibox is a twitch-heavy action game crafted for the hardcore audience."
Grr Argh. Arrrgh! The number of times you will end up
dying on level one alone should be enough to persuade
you that this game is not for the casual gamer.
The moment you go into the game, it instantly starts with
a tutorial which shows you what to do. But it's
such a short learning curve that the tutorial doesn't
help that much. How you do learn is from failing.
Constantly failing, until you get it right.
It's good for a
patient gamer, so if you're prepared to spend a lot of
time trying to perfect your levels, and to fail them,
over and over again, and control your inner
rage, then I would recommend it. If you are a completist,
determined to win at any game you play no matter how
difficult it is, I recommend it.
The controls are not perfect - I couldn't use my Gamepad
for it so I had to use my keyboard, but it could be
a bug from my end.
It's quite a simple game graphics wise. It is
effective with how they are utilised. The game mechanics
are also deceptively simple: you avoid black lines and collect cubes until you finish
the level. However, there is maybe 10% of people who
will be able to complete level one quickly. It will test
your ability to perservere and your self control.
The music is very addictive, and again the sound will
test your self control, since you are, lets not lie,
you ARE going to hear the words "Level One," in a cool
female voice, followed by "Game over," over and over again.
And then with the other levels. Over and over again.
Good luck.
Do note, that if you're a person who has trouble with
motion sickness in games, I wouldn't play this straight
away, or for extended periods of time.

Please be warned. You will get annoyed. Tears will be shed.
Gamepads may or may not be thrown at the wall.
But you will be deeply satisfied with each level you
complete.

Do you miss those grand old days of cursing the rng with your friends on Mario Party. Do you miss going all or nothing to screw over your friends or yourself in Dokapon kingdom? Well then 100% Orange Juice is the game for you.
In truth though, dokapon kingdom is a game simple enough to jump online and chat but complex enough to make some meaningful decisions. 4 players travel around a board with spaces for collecting or losing stars, fighting enemies, and collecting cards. your goal is to acheive "norma" by either meeting a quota of stars (which you lose half of when knocked out), or acheiving the harder goal of battle victories (which can't be removed). you must land on a player starting space to move to the next level of norma, and the first to achieve the sixth level wins.
Adding some customization is the different characters, which all have unique attributes of Health, Attack Power, Defense, and Dodge, as well as unique passives such as a higher chance to revive after KO. Characters must be unlocked through the story mode or via unique character DLC, with your first character being the one you start your story with. Each player also builds a 10 card deck of collectible cards, which all get shuffled together with 8 character unique hyper cards to be drawn in the game. This way players with larger collections will be drawing from the same pool as other players.
All in All 100% Orange Juice is a game that will be most enjoyed by party game fans, followers of RNJesus, and fans of japanese artstyle and voice acting. Fans of developer Orange Juices previous games will also find some added value.

Do you like board games? If so, you should consider this game. 100% orange juice is a game filled with so much randomness, it would make TF2 random crit haters cry tears of blood. With just enough skill involved to make it feel like you can control the outcome, 100% orange juice is a game you will keep coming back to, no matter how many friends you want to punch in the face.

My favourite board game on Steam. Ideal for casual online sessions with total strangers.

You may be thinking "How does a drink become a game?", well first its not a drink, and second it just does 'cause the game mascot Poppo says so.
Back to the topic at hand, 100% Orange Juice is a 4-player board game unlike any other, many people might compare it to Mario Party or other such party games but you shouldn't, its in a league of its own.
Rules are rather simple, reach your 5-stock goal and reach a homebase to win, simple?, not in 100%OJ it isn't.
In order to get stocks you must select a goal to reach first, at the start of each game everyone must collect 10 stars *unless you buy a certain dlc character*, once you got the goal and hit a base you earn a stock, you then select your next goal to reach and repeat the process, untill you clear the fifth stock goal and be the first to win by reaching a homebase.
The goals you can choose from are Stars and Wins, Stars are like currency you earn every turn and from landing on bonus squares or from effects of cards, which i will get to later, Wins are earned by defeating your oppenants in battle, either by landing on a battle square or choosing to fight your oppenants you pass by, certain oppenants earn more wins than others, Battle square monsters earn 1 win, oppenants you battle by choice earn you 2 wins, and Boss squares earn you 3 wins.
You can also turn the tide of battle, buff yourself before a movement or even effect some spaces you land on with cards, some cards however cost stars to use or even require a certain stock level to reach first before you can play them, nevertheless they are a helpful hand to you or even your oppenant when you need them *or not*.
There are modes in 100%OJ to enjoy but stick around the gameboard theme, play Story Mode to unravel how certain people got dragged into this madness, Single Player to come up with deck ideas or to try new characters outs, and when your satisfied with your result take it Online agaisnt the world where you can earn levels and rewards for your efforts.
A fun game to play *or torment* with your friends, or even to make new friends Online, 100% Orange Juice will always be a ideal game to have around when your lost for ideas what to do.

Endless Legend (EL) is a very ambitious simultaneously turn based new 4X (eXplore, eXpand, eXploit, eXterminate) strategy game in a fantasy setting by Amplitude studios (Endless Legend, Dungeon of the Endless). The general setting is unusual, as you're stranded on the planet Auriga that has been a favoured laboratory of a powerful precursor race, the Endless, until they erased themselves from existence in a large civil war.
Now, you take control of one out of 8 standard factions or any custom faction you create in an editor, using the basic gameplay of one of the 8 with some modifiers. Your goal is to survive as Auriga is slowly drifting towards an everlasting winter that will snuff out all life left on its surface. There are several victory conditions you can fulfill, ranging from "bucket"-type conditions like gathering enough currency or being the highest in score at a configurable turn limit to fulfilling a quest and building an expensive wonder, exterminating all concurrents or researching yourself to victory. Not all of these victory conditions are equally fun to reach as "filling a bucket" can be quite tedious, but the different factions are also specialised at reaching different victory conditions.
And this is where EL is ambitious in the sense that its 8 factions are very asymmetrically designed:
- The Wild Walkers are the not so usual Elves of the game, using woods to boost their industrial proficiency. They get to be the production powerhouse of the game.
- The Vaulters are the survivors of the Dungeon of the Endless game, stranded on the planet. Hightech-dwarfs of a sort with heavy armor and the best science output.
- The Rowing Clans are supposed to be the traders of the planet. They cannot declare war, are better than the NSA at finding out who's selling or buying what to a common marketplace you can get access to by research, and can actually even trade-ban people, bleeding them dry, economically.
- The Drakken are the peacekeepers, a draconid race interested in achieving diplomatic victory by using their influence to force whole empires into peace or alliance with them.
- The Ardent Mages can use spells on the map and in combat. Given enough currency, a weak army of them can still beat a superior foe with enough magic support fire.
- The Necrophage do not do anything but feed, war and reproduce. Peace is not an option, as is not conquering. The Zergs of the planet, indeed.
- The Broken Lords are living armors thinking of themselves as paladins and leeching life like vampires. Lorewise, one of my favourites, their gameplay is centered on currency to buy population with.
- The Cultists of the Eternal End have only one city and expand by converting minor faction villages across the planet to generate troops for them and to harvest resources for them.
In general, this asymmetry is what makes the game nice, but it is also its vulnerability. As each faction plays differently, the AI also has to account for that. During the Early Access phase, the AI made huge jumps and has become a threat to the unwary at higher difficulty levels, now, but still fails in the endgame. It doesn't recognize that, given it is close to winning, the human player in the game will go to lengths to eradicate them. On the other hand, in the beginning, different AI personalities shine through. Around the Ardent Mages, there's always a lot of scorched earth destroyed minor faction villages, while Wild Walkers spread and pacify, instead. I'm quite confident that this will improve, further, but I rate what's present, now.
Therefore I downright recommend to play this game in multiplayer. The simultaneous turns allow for fast games, compared to other titles. You can set turn timers and therefore force people to be fast, or give each and everyone as much time as they want, but a long game would last 4 hours, at most, on fast speed settings.
Even there, though, the asymmetry of the game design has its dangers. You can equip your units with better and better equipment through the ages, having to use strategic resources on the map to get the very best, but there's a clear preference for some attributes being far better than others. Some units you gain by assimilating minor factions (you can then build their units and get some bonus per controlled village of that faction) are better than standard units and certainly better than most other units on the planet. I'm thinking of e.g. Kazanjii demons or Haunts of the Ended here, both having a chain hit special ability.
One thing I have to add about the techtree: It is not linear, there's no clear progression. In each "era", you have to choose at least x technologies, then you progress to the next era. Each time you research something, the cost for the next research increases, no matter the era its out of.
Overall, the game has a lot of depth for someone who favours empire management over combat. There's still lots of balancing and AI-tuning to do, but the game is fun and I recommend it.
